成化二十三年進士登科錄

玉音

成化二十三年三月十二日，太子少保、禮部尚書臣周洪謨等於奉天門奏，為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百五十一名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士萬安等五十三員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士萬安〔戊辰進士〕。
光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太傅、户部尚書、謹身殿大學士劉吉〔戊辰進士〕。
資善大夫、太子少保、兵部尚書兼翰林院學士尹直〔甲戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of the Metropolitan Graduates of the Twenty-third Year of Chenghua (1487)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the twelfth day of the third month of the twenty-third year of Chenghua, your servant Zhou Hongmo, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, and others memorialized at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations: “In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the empire, 351 candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we request the appointment of fifty-three officials as Readers and other examination functionaries, including Wan An, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The grades of status conferred upon the metropolitan graduates shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially prescribed by Emperor Taizu Gao: in the first class, three men shall be selected according to precedent. The first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a; they shall be granted the distinction ‘Presented Scholar with Honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and be granted ‘Presented Scholar Background.’ Those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and be granted ‘Equivalent to Presented Scholar Background.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respect this.

Readers

Wan An, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Pillar of State, was Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.〕

Liu Ji, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Pillar of State, was Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.〕

Yin Zhi, Grand Master for Fostering Virtue, was Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.〕

Huang Jing, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year. Ni Yue, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year.

Fan Zhu, Gentleman for Rendering Service and Investigating Censor for the Zhejiang Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year. Zhu Zan, Gentleman for Scholarly Service and Investigating Censor for the Guangxi Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Script Reception Officials
Dong Yue, Reader of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year. Jiang Lan, Hanlin Academy Compiler and Gentleman for Scholarly Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

三月十八日
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the twenty-third year of Chenghua (1487), all the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy questions.

On the morning of the seventeenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard arrayed the ceremonial insignia and guards along the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the successful candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites reverently carried the yellow announcement of results, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate. After the announcement had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with a ceremonial parasol and retinue.

On the eighteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…a banquet was granted at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, they went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the rites.
On the nineteenth day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed upon the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twentieth day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of thanks for imperial favor.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the first-ranked graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites memorialized the throne, requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the National University and inscribe their names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the designation “jinshi with honors.”

Fei Hong, registered in a civilian household in Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zichong; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Rongzu; his grandfather was Yingqi, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father was Fan; and his mother was née Yu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xian, and his younger brothers were Ning, Huan, Mi, Wan, Yu, Yu, Cai, Zong, and Mi. His wife was née Pu. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chun, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Renzhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Keming; his grandfather was Gang, a Station Master; his father was Gui, an Assistant Subprefect and formerly an Investigating Censor; and his mother was née Deng. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brother was Tai. His wife was née Jian. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Rui, registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bangxiang; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Boshan; his grandfather was Junsheng; his father was Gao, formerly a Registrar; and his mother was née Xia. Both his parents were living. His younger brothers were Zan, Chen, Jin (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), Xun, and Lian. His wife was née Huang. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Kai, registered in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhengzhi; he ranked twenty-first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijian, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Wengong; his father was Chunfang; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fuzhi, and his wife was née Mao. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xi, registered in Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingxin; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was forty years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youren; his grandfather was Chaozhong; his father was Yuan; and his mother was née Zhu 祝. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lin, and his wife was née Zhu 朱. He placed fortieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Yuan, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Benqing; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongwen; his grandfather was Tingjie; his father was Shichun; and his mother was née Li. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Benkuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Chao, and his wife was née Hu. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周夔〔貫江西吉安府廬陵縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字甫敬，行三，年三十五，三月十八日生〕。曾祖思榮，祖彥政，父賓，母龍氏。慈侍下，兄瑚、璉，弟斐，娶王氏。江西鄉試第十六名，會試第一百六十七名。

任倫〔貫河南睢陽衛軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字秉元，行一，年三十二，五月初九日生〕。曾祖宣，祖質，父廣，母王氏。具慶下，娶高氏。河南鄉試第二十九名，會試第三百四十六名。

陳欽〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣人，南京欽天監籍，應天府學生，治書經，字亮之，行七，年二十四，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖一廉，祖嵩，父瓛〔教諭〕，母劉氏。重慶下，兄鐸、銃、銀、鉞、鎬〔同科進士〕、鎧，弟銳，娶蔣氏，繼娶王氏。應天府鄉試第三十七名，會試第十九名。
translation_en:
Zhou Kui, a student of the Imperial University, belonged to the civilian register of Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Fujing, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sirong, his grandfather Yanzheng, and his father Bin; his mother was née Long. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Hu and Lian, and his younger brother was Fei. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yu, a student of the Imperial University, belonged to the military register of Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zixian, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiliang; his grandfather Gongzheng was granted the honorary title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, and his father Zhi was a Director in that ministry. His father’s former wife, née Zhou, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother was née Liu 留. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Fu, Gui, Sheng, and Hua 𠤎 [?]. He married a woman née Guan. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Lun, a student of the Imperial University, belonged to the military register of Suiyang Guard, Henan. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Bingyuan, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Guang; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Gao. He placed twenty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 346th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qin was a native of Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered with the Nanjing Directorate of Astronomy, and a student of the Yingtian Prefectural School. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Liangzhi, and he ranked seventh among his brothers. He was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yilian, his grandfather Song, and his father Huan, a School Instructor; his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Duo, Chong, Yin, Yue, Hao (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), and Kai; his younger brother was Rui. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊瑛〔貫直隸蘇州府嘉定縣，民籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字潤卿，行一，年三十五，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖彥英，祖豫〔教諭〕，父復，前母張氏，母崔氏。慈侍下，弟瑢、珪、璋，娶金氏。應天府鄉試第二十名，會試第三百十四名。

translation_en:
Wang Hongru 王鴻儒, courtesy name Maoxue, was registered in Nanyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, in a military household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun, his grandfather Cheng, his father Ben, and his mother née Si; both parents were living; his younger brother was Hongjian, and his wife was née Wu; he placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Wei 董威, courtesy name Deyu, was registered in Wei County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged twenty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Xing, his father Xian, and his mother née Liu; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Wen, Zhang, Fu, and Qing, his younger brother was Yi, and his wife was née Gao; he placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ying 楊瑛, courtesy name Runqing, was registered in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household; he was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanying, his grandfather Yu〔Instructor〕, and his father Fu; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Cui; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Rong, Gui, and Zhang, and his wife was née Jin; he placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Mian 蔣冕, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, in a civilian household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged twenty-five, born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guan〔Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice〕, his grandfather An, and his father Liang〔District Magistrate〕; his legal mother was née Guo and his birth mother née Chen; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers are listed as Bian, Sheng〔a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort〕, Bian [?—the name is repeated], and Bing, his younger brother was Gong 㫒, and his wife was née Chen; he placed first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Han, of Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weirong, and he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins. He was twenty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizheng, his grandfather Yue, and his father Luan; his mother was née Qiu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mian and Han, and his wife was née Zhu 諸. He placed forty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Tong was originally from Dayu County, Nan’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongbo, and he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanxin, his grandfather Fuxian, and his father Rong; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jian, his younger brothers were Da and Xian, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hao was originally from Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was registered with the Nanjing Directorate of Astronomy. He was a student of the Yingtian Prefectural School and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongzhi, and he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins. He was twenty-six, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yilian, his grandfather Song, and his father Huan 〔School Instructor〕; his mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Duo, Xian, Yin, and Yue; his younger brothers were Kai, Qin 〔a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort〕, and Rui. His wife was née Fang. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Heng, of Shanghe County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yongtai, and he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-three, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixin, his grandfather Shengju, and his father Bin 〔Registrar〕; his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Mao, and his wife was née Sun. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 333rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

葉紳〔貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字廷縉，行一，年四十四，六月初四日生〕。曾祖仲賓〔大使〕，祖蕙，父芳〔副理問〕，母朱氏。具慶下，弟紘、縯、緤〔貢士〕，娶褚氏。應天府鄉試第十六名，會試第一百六名。

蔡欽〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字懋鄰，行一，年四十三，十二月十三日生〕。曾祖伯顏，祖叔孟，父軾，母戚氏。具慶下，弟鑑、鍊〔貢士〕、錄、錦、鏞，娶吳氏，繼娶董氏。浙江鄉試第四名，會試第九十四名。
translation_en:
Ye Shen 葉紳, courtesy name Tingjin, was from Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, with civilian household registration; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-four, born on the fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongbin, a Commissioner; his grandfather was Hui; his father was Fang, a Deputy Judicial Officer; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hong, Yan, and Xie (a tribute scholar, gongshi). He married a woman née Chu and placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Zheng 歐鉦, courtesy name Shizhen, was from Meizhou, Sichuan, with civilian household registration; he was a cultivated talent (xiucai) of the Hanlin Academy specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Junxiang; his grandfather was Bin; and his father was Lian, an Investigating Censor. His legal mother, née Yang, and his birth mother, née Huang, were both posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Rui, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and his younger brother was Qian, a Clerk. He married a woman née Yu and placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Shen 屈伸, courtesy name Yinzhi, was from Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered region, with civilian household registration; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Guineng; his grandfather was Qing; his father was Zhong; his mother was née Zhang; and his stepmother was née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zheng, Duan, Fang, and Kai. He married a woman née Bian and placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Qin 蔡欽, courtesy name Maolin, was from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, with civilian household registration; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Boyan; his grandfather was Shumeng; his father was Shi; and his mother was née Qi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian, Lian (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Lu, Jin, and Yong. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Dong, and placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

程昊〔貫直隸徽州府祁門縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字時亨，行一，年四十六，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖景華，祖顯〔左春坊左司直郎兼翰林院檢討〕，父貫，母胡氏，繼母謝氏。具慶下，弟旻，娶汪氏。應天府鄉試第八十二名，會試第九名。
translation_en:
Tu Jin, courtesy name Bangyu, was from Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boshan; his grandfather, Junsheng; his father, Zhang, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rui, a provincial graduate (juren), Zan, and Chen; his younger brothers were Xiang and Lian. His wife was née Zhou. He ranked forty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 325th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zongren, courtesy name Tiyuan, was from Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Duo, a Vice Commissioner; his father, Gang, an Official for Righteousness, an honorary designation; and his mother, née Song. Both parents were living. His younger brother Zongyi also held the honorary designation Official for Righteousness. His wife was née Bian; he subsequently married a woman née Zhu. He ranked sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Lun, courtesy name Chaoyan, was from Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sicheng; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Xin; and his mother, née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shou, Ji, Xu, and Shen. His wife was née Hu. He ranked second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Hao, courtesy name Shiheng, was from Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged forty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghua; his grandfather, Xian, Left Rectifier in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his father, Guan; his mother, née Hu; and his stepmother, née Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Min. His wife was née Wang. He ranked eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Jinglun, registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruxue; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Xuanfang; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Huang. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brother was Silun, and his wife was née Yu. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Da, registered in a civilian household in Da County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Guiling, his grandfather Xu, and his father Fuzu; his father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Siyi, and his younger brothers were Di, Kui, and Ti. His wife was née Wei; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chaoyang, registered in a military household of Xunan Guard, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingfeng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Mao, a Company Commander granted the cap and sash of official status; and his father was Jie. His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living, and his wife was née Yu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Teng Bin, a native of Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a military household of the Jinchi military office in Yunnan. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiuzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Yong, and his father Qing; his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Song, who had been granted the cap and sash of official status under the applicable regulations, and Gui; his younger brothers were Qi and Ji. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫濡〔貫直隸鳳陽府鳳陽縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字幼真，行一，年三十八，二月十二日生〕。曾祖通吉〔聽選官〕，祖文賦，父寧，母陸氏。具慶下，娶徐氏。應天府鄉試第五十一名，會試第三十七名。

張賁〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣人，錦衣衛鎮撫司軍籍，國子生，治書經，字希臯，行一，年二十九，正月初七日生〕。曾祖以勗〔冠帶官〕，祖德崇〔贈刑部員外郎〕，父玘〔按察使〕，母李氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母梁氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，弟賔、貫、貢、賚，娶康氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第七十名。

賈澄〔貫湖廣辰州衛，官籍，國子生，治易經，字廉夫，行二，年二十九，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖忠，祖文立，父霖〔百戶〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄洪〔百戶〕、潤，弟清、瀾，娶向氏。湖廣鄉試第五十八名，會試第三百四十一名。

彭崑〔貫福建建寧府崇安縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字良玉，行一，年四十五，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖明之，祖仲仁，父成福，母陳氏。慈侍下，弟嵩、崙、嶽、山，娶楊氏。福建鄉試第八十名，會試第二百七十一名。
translation_en:
Sun Ru, courtesy name Youzhen, was registered in Fengyang County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tongji, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his grandfather was Wenfu; his father was Ning; and his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ben, courtesy name Xigao, was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, registered in a military household under the Disciplinary Office of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yixu, an official granted the cap and girdle of official status; his grandfather was Dechong, posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Qi, a Surveillance Commissioner; his mother was née Li, posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; and his stepmother was née Liang, granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were Bin, Guan, Gong, and Lai. His wife was née Kang. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Cheng, courtesy name Lianfu, was registered at Chenzhou Guard in Huguang in an official household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Wenli; his father was Lin, a Company Commander; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hong, a Company Commander, and Run; his younger brothers were Qing and Lan. His wife was née Xiang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 341st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Kun, courtesy name Liangyu, was registered in Chong'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Mingzhi; his grandfather was Zhongren; his father was Chengfu; and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Song, Lun, Yue, and Shan. His wife was née Yang. He placed eightieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
黃穆〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字子敬，行五，年四十三，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖則誠，祖德敷〔贈監察御史〕，父譽〔布政司左參政〕，前母鄭氏〔贈孺人〕，母林氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄鐸〔刑部主事〕、銳、和、銓，弟秩〔貢士〕、秀〔貢士〕、鈺，娶林氏。福建鄉試第二名，會試第六十二名。

范玶〔貫江西饒州府浮梁縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字文潤，行十一，年三十五，十二月二十八日生〕。曾祖伯全，祖思禮〔義官〕，父傑〔進士〕，母方氏。慈侍下，兄瑾、璨，弟玖、琯、璥，娶戴氏。江西鄉試第八十一名，會試第二百三十六名。

陳玉〔貫直隸涿鹿中衛官籍，涿州學生，治禮記，字潤夫，行一，年三十七，二月十九日生〕。曾祖峻〔衛鎮撫〕，祖信，父通，母劉氏。具慶下，弟玘，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百三十九名。

陳仁〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子居，行七，年三十四，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖孟庸，祖允德，父舜衡，母吳氏。具慶下，娶李氏。福建鄉試第一名，會試第四十七名。
translation_en:
Huang Mu 黃穆, of civilian household registration in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked fifth in birth order, was aged forty-three, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zecheng; his grandfather, Defu, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; and his father, Yu 譽, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father's former wife, née Zheng, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his mother, née Lin, was granted the same title. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Duo, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, Rui, He, and Quan; his younger brothers were Zhi and Xiu, both tribute students (gongshi), and Yu 鈺. He married a woman née Lin. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Ping 范玶, of civilian household registration in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenrun; he ranked eleventh in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boquan; his grandfather, Sili, held honorary official status for charitable contributions; his father, Jie, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); and his mother was née Fang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Jin and Can, and his younger brothers were Jiu, Guan, and Jing. He married a woman née Dai. He placed eighty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yu 陳玉, of official household registration in Zhuolu Central Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Zhuozhou government school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Runfu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, a Guard Disciplinary Officer; his grandfather was Xin; his father was Tong; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were still living. His younger brother was Qi, and he married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ren 陳仁, of military household registration in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziju; he ranked seventh in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengyong; his grandfather was Yunde; his father was Shunheng; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were still living. He married a woman née Li. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳邦弼〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，府學增廣生，治詩經，字惟忠，行三，年二十三，十月二十四日生〕。曾祖處恭，祖齡，父定〔教諭〕，母吳氏。重慶下，兄邦直〔貢士〕、邦榮〔會試中式舉人〕，娶魯氏。浙江鄉試第六名，會試第二十四名。

傅珪〔貫直隸保定府清苑縣，軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字邦瑞，行一，年二十九，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖貴，祖信〔主簿〕，父泰〔國子生〕，母劉氏。具慶下，弟璋、瓚、琮、珩，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第八十二名。

萬弘璧〔貫四川眉州，官籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷瑞，行一，年二十二，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖林〔贈光祿大夫、柱國、太子太保、吏部尚書兼謹身殿大學士〕，祖安〔光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士〕，父翼〔嘉議大夫、兵部侍郎〕，母趙氏〔封恭人〕。重慶下，弟弘瓚、弘琬、弘珩〔中書舍人〕、弘珍，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第十八名，會試第一百十一名。

鄧琛〔貫廣東廣州府東莞縣，竈籍，國子生，治書經，字貢甫，行三，年四十一，二月十八日生〕。曾祖國錡，祖組〔知縣〕，父惠，母張氏。慈侍下，兄瓛、珏，弟玹，娶秦氏。廣東鄉試第七十五名，會試第九十一名。
translation_en:
Chen Bangbi, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weizhong, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Chugong, his grandfather Ling, his father Ding (School Instructor), and his mother née Wu; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Bangzhi (a tribute scholar) and Bangrong (a provincial graduate who had passed the Metropolitan Examination), and his wife was née Lu; he placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Gui, registered in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bangrui, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Xin (Registrar), his father Tai (a student of the Directorate of Education), and his mother née Liu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhang, Zan, Cong, and Heng, and his wife was née Wang; he placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Hongbi, registered in Meizhou, Sichuan, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingrui, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-two, born on the third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Lin (posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel concurrently serving as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Scrupulous Conduct); his grandfather was An (Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of the Flowery Canopy); his father was Yi (Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Vice Minister of War), and his mother was née Zhao (granted the title Lady of Respect). His parents and at least one grandparent were living; his younger brothers were Hongzan, Hongwan, Hongheng (a Secretariat Drafter), and Hongzhen, and his wife was née Yang. He placed eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Chen, registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongfu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Guoqi, his grandfather Zu (District Magistrate), his father Hui, and his mother née Zhang; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Huan and Jue, his younger brother was Xuan, and his wife was née Qin; he placed seventy-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu De, courtesy name Yiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Rong was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Qin was a Prefect. His father was Ying, and his mother was née Hao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhong and En, and he married a woman née Liu. He placed thirtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Fu, courtesy name Shunxun, was a native of Qiantang County, Zhejiang, registered in an official household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Derun was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing. His grandfather Zi’an was granted the title of Academician of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently holding an unspecified post in a Secretariat of the Heir Apparent [?], and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing. His father Qian was Minister of Rites at Nanjing, posthumously appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Wenxi. His father’s former wife, née Yao, and his mother, née Guo, were both posthumously granted the title of Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Yue was Right Vice Minister of Rites; his younger brothers were Shan and Ze. He married a woman née Yu. He placed forty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hua Luan, courtesy name Bozhan, was registered in a military household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A department school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty, and born on the eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather Qi was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His father Zhongxian was a Prefect. His mother, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren), and his stepmother, née Pan, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were both living. His younger brother was Yue, and he married a woman née Wang. He placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan, courtesy name Tingmian, was registered in a military household in Ninghai Department, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhongli, his grandfather was Zeng, and his father Qi was a County Magistrate. His father’s former wife was née Sun; his mother, née Zhang, was a chaste widow. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wan Fu 萬福 was registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Jichong and ranked tenth in family order. He was forty-one years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Junqing; his grandfather, Dequan; and his father, Yuanhe, a prefectural school instructor. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Niu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xian, Rong, Hua, Gao, Sheng, and Fang; his younger brother was Jide. His wife was née Rao. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Jie 董傑 was registered in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Wanying and ranked eighth in family order. He was forty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhizhong; his grandfather, Yuanliang; and his father, Zhidao, posthumously granted the title of Case Reviewer. His mother, née Xiao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of the Ninth Rank. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qian, Zhen, Wan, Liang, Chang, Sheng, Hui, Gang, and Qun; his younger brothers were Zhuo, Kan, Ti, and Cheng. His wife was née Wang. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yan 吳儼 was registered in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Kewen and ranked third in family order. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Yizhong, was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Yu, held that office. His father was Jing, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Xu 許 (a different surname from his mother's 徐). His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Wei and Ren; his younger brothers were Yi, Jian, and Shi. His wife was née Shen. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Tong 趙仝 was registered in Shan Subprefecture, Henan Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Jibei and ranked third in family order. He was forty-seven years old, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sanweng; his grandfather, Lin; and his father, Xi, an Instructor in the School of Yin-Yang Studies, granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel. His legal mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of the Sixth Rank; his birth mother was née Liang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wen, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Wu, an Instructor in the School of Yin-Yang Studies. His wife was née Pang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

余徵〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，平海衛學民生，治詩經，字弘貴，行一，年四十三，正月十二日生〕。曾祖俊卿〔贈按察司僉事〕，祖文〔前知府〕，父廷列，母彭氏。永感下，弟珫，娶林氏。福建鄉試第七十九名，會試第三百十七名。
translation_en:
Ma Yu 馬輿, courtesy name Liangzai, was registered in a military officer household of the Jiaxing Defense Battalion under the Suzhou Guard in the directly administered territory, and was a military student at the Jiaxing County School. He specialized in the Book of Documents, was first in birth order, and was aged forty, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Andao; his grandfather, Daorong; his father, Xiang; and his mother, née Ye. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Lun and Quan, and his wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Dan 凃旦, courtesy name Qingyuan, was registered in an artisan household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes, was sixth in birth order, and was aged twenty-four, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guosheng; his grandfather, Yongzai, was granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Guan, was a Prefect. His mother, née Xu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren), and his stepmother, née Zhu, was granted the same title. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother, Jingsheng, was a District Magistrate; his younger brothers were Zao, Jingyan, and Xu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Di 王迪, courtesy name Yunji, was registered in a civilian household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, was seventh in birth order, and was aged thirty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Guizong; his father, Duan; and his mother, née Lü. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Da and his younger brother was Kui; his wife was née Chen. He placed fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Zheng 余徵, courtesy name Honggui, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a civilian student at the Pinghai Guard School. He specialized in the Book of Odes, was first in birth order, and was aged forty-three, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Junqing, was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather, Wen, was a former Prefect; his father was Tinglie; and his mother was née Peng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Chong, and his wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉約〔貫山東兖州府東平州東阿縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字博之，行七，年二十九，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖思明，祖璉〔教諭〕，父觀〔七品散官〕，母蘇氏。具慶下，兄紀、經、紓、綸、繼、純，弟綬、綺、緩、緯、綰，娶徐氏。山東鄉試第十九名，會試第二百九十九名。

姜麟〔貫浙江金華府蘭谿縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字仁夫，行六十七，年三十五，四月初一日生〕。曾祖仲威，祖仕毅〔府經歷，贈知州〕，父連〔知府〕，母嚴氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄芝、鈍、鉤、茂，弟芳、萱、鳳、錦、騶、盛、熊、鐩、龍、驥，娶盛氏。浙江鄉試第十八名，會試第一百三十四名。
translation_en:
Shao Tang, of a military household registered in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Min’ai; he ranked first in his family’s birth order, was thirty-six, and was born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kexiang, a Battalion Commander; his grandfather was Zhongji; his father was Zongben; and his mother was née Sang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brother was Fei. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed 123rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 97th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Duo, of a civilian household registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Ruyuan County school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Daoming; he ranked first in his family’s birth order, was thirty-four, and was born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Suizhen; his grandfather was Ding; his father was Yongxiang; and his mother was née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Rui, Jian, and Lu. He married a woman née Lu 盧. He placed 17th in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yue, of a civilian household registered in Dong’e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bozhi; he ranked seventh in his family’s birth order, was twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siming; his grandfather was Lian, an Instructor; his father was Guan, holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Su. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji 紀, Jing, Shu 紓, Lun, Ji 繼, and Chun; his younger brothers were Shou, Qi, Huan, Wei, and Wan. He married a woman née Xu. He placed 19th in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Lin, of a civilian household registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked sixty-seventh in his family’s birth order, was thirty-five, and was born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongwei; his grandfather was Shiyi, a Prefectural Registrar posthumously granted the title of Subprefect; his father was Lian, a Prefect; and his mother was née Yan, granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhi, Dun, Gou, and Mao; his younger brothers were Fang, Xuan, Feng, Jin, Zou, Sheng, Xiong, Sui, Long, and Ji. He married a woman née Sheng. He placed 18th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Han, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kezhao; he ranked ninth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Boxing; his grandfather, Yan, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Zizhi, and his mother was née Luo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Wen and Jian, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenxiang, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tianrui; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Yuan, was honorarily appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His grandfather, Zhengfang, was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, advanced to the honorary ranks of Grand Master for Administrative Service and Minister for Proper Governance. His father, Guan, was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and his mother, née Zhao, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Wenzhen, Wenqin, Wenbiao, and Wenchang, and his wife was née Zou. He placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Jing, registered in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chengzhi; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Jingliang, was a County Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Heng, received the same titles posthumously. His father, Zhong, held the honorary titles Grand Master for Aid in Virtue and Senior Minister for Proper Governance and was the retired Minister of War, advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness. His father's former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady; his mother, née Bao, was granted the same title. His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Gang, a tribute scholar; Ji, a Daoist Registrar; and Lun. His younger brothers were Shou, a Battalion Commander; Wei; Yun; and Shen. He married a woman née Zhao as his subsequent wife. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhong, registered in Ninghai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shizhong; he ranked seventh in his family and was forty-five years old, born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gongmeng; his grandfather, Wenkui, was an Honored Commoner; his father was Zongyao; his mother was née Ren, and his stepmother was née Dai. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Menghong, Mengxun, Mengliang, and Mengkuan; his younger brothers were Mengjun, Menghuang, Mengjian, Mengqi, Mengqian, and Mengkai. His wife was née Yang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊茂仁〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字志道，行二二二二，年二十八，十月十七日生〕。曾祖九疇，祖自懲〔贈侍講學士〕，父守陳〔少詹事兼侍講學士〕，母丁氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄茂元〔按察司副使〕、茂貞，弟茂禮、茂行、茂清，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第五十名，會試第二百八十三名。

熊祥〔貫江西豐城縣金吾貴州鎮遠府偏橋長官司，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字文應，行二，年三十二，正月十八日生〕。曾祖國用，祖本靜，父鼎，嫡母涂氏，生母羅氏。慈侍下，弟裕，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第九十三名，會試第二百四十一名。
translation_en:
Yang Maoren, courtesy name Zhidao, was from Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was twenty-eight, was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month, and had a family birth-order ranking recorded as “二二二二” [?]. His great-grandfather was Jiuchou; his grandfather, Zicheng, was posthumously appointed Expositor-in-waiting; his father, Shouchen, was Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Expositor-in-waiting; and his mother, née Ding, held the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Maoyuan, Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission, and Maozhen; his younger brothers were Maoli, Maoxing, and Maoqing. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Fei, courtesy name Yucheng, was from Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a medical household. A medical student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth in family birth order, was twenty-two, and was born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather, Wang, was posthumously appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals; his father, Lan, was Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission; and his mother, née Yang, held the title Lady of Suitability. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Sen, Kai (an Imperial University student), Bin, Ben, and Gai; his younger brothers were Xiang, Gui, Ji, Mo, Cai, and Ke. He married a woman née Gao. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Shi, courtesy name Shicheng, was from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. An added-quota student at the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fourth in family birth order, was thirty-six, and was born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Bai; his grandfather, Yong; his father, Jin; his mother, née Shen; and his stepmother, née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xian, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and Rong; his younger brothers were Yin, Fu, and Huan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Xiang, courtesy name Wenying, was a civilian registrant whose place of origin is given as Fengcheng County, Jiangxi, followed by “Jinwu” [?] and Pianqiao Native Chief’s Office, Zhenyuan Prefecture, Guizhou. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family birth order, was thirty-two, and was born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Guoyong; his grandfather, Benjing; his father, Ding; his legal mother, née Tu; and his birth mother, née Luo. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Yu. He married a woman née Li. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xuan, registered in Yi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunji, and he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-three, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kui; his grandfather, Huai, was a Magistrate; his father was Zhishan; his mother was née Shu, and his stepmother was also née Shu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Cheng, Sui, and Jie, and his younger brothers were Yu, Long, and Chang. His wife was née Shu. He ranked forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jin, registered in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shangjiong, and he was second in birth order, aged forty, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yande; his grandfather was Fang; his father was Qiong; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jian, and his younger brothers were Yi, Yue, and Tang. His wife was née Yao. He ranked ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Kui, registered in Yutian County, Ji Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Daoheng, and he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deyuan; his grandfather was Sangong; his father was Shen; his mother was née Sun, and his stepmother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Da, and his wife was née Zou. He ranked eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Gongfu, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Liangchen, and he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhong; his grandfather was Zizheng; his father was Zhen, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His first wife was née Song, and his subsequent wife was née Wang. He ranked eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Ju, courtesy name Mengxian, was registered in a civilian household in Luancheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Gong, his father Cai, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fei and Jue, and his wife was née Liang. He placed eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Feng, courtesy name Yingshao, was registered in a military household in Li County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiyou; his grandfather Jie was posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; and his father Zheng was Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His father's former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his mother, also née Zhang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother Luan was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Hong, a Seal Keeper, and Peng. His wife was née Chen. He placed eighteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Ren, courtesy name Xingshu, was registered in a civilian household in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi'an, his grandfather Daoyin, his father Jingyuan, his mother née Ye, and his stepmother née Feng. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Lin, and Zhi, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Lun, courtesy name Tianxu, was a native of Anyue County, Sichuan, registered in a military household in Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Long, his grandfather Ying, his father Hong, a Commissioner, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ru and Fu; his younger brothers were Jian, Ji, and Zhuan. His wife was née Li. He placed fortieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Yan, of military household registration in Fucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zaiwen; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benchu, his grandfather You, and his father Zhen; his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xuan and Zan; his younger brothers were Jing, Fan, Yu, Pu, Rong, Xuan, and Ji. He married a woman née Chang and subsequently a woman née Lu. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Zicong, of civilian household registration in Guangping County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shunda; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather De was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing; his grandfather Lian was a student of the Directorate of Education. His father was Zhao, and his mother was née Fan; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bingyi and Zhou, and his younger brother was Yue. He married a woman née Jin. He placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Jian, a native of Shanyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, Zhili, registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guaming [?]; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Menghe, and his father Yiwen, an honorary official; his mother was née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Gao, Yi, Ming, Qin, Yong, Yue, and Zhen. He married a woman née Ke. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Jun, of civilian household registration in Tiantai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xizhe; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-four, and was born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deshen; his grandfather Yan and father Rong were both Instructors. His mother was née Pan; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Han and Fu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Qing, courtesy name Tianxi, was from Longqing Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region and was registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather, Congshan, was a Station Master; and his father, Xuan, was a District Magistrate. His father's former wife was née Mu, and his mother was née Sheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ning, a Station Master, and Tai. He married a woman née Lü and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed 101st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Duancheng, courtesy name Xuepu, was from Wuzhi County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, and was registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rongzu [?]; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Youzhi; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hai, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Qing. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed twenty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Xi, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was from Wuzhi County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, and was registered in a military household. A military student at the school of the Wanquan Regional Military Commission, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked tenth among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiaoxian; his grandfather was Xin; his father was Heng; and his mother was née Hua. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yu, Can, and Xuan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Li, courtesy name Yonghe, was a native of Liangxiang County, Shuntian Prefecture, registered in an officer household of the Yongning Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shaosan. His grandfather, Ying, was a Battalion Commander, posthumously granted the title General of Military Strategy (Wulüe Jiangjun). His father, Gang, was a Battalion Commander awarded the same title. His mother, née Liu, was granted the title Lady of Suitability (Yiren). Both parents were living. His elder brother, Fu, and younger brother, Zhen, were Battalion Commanders; his other younger brothers were Xiang and Qi. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Xia. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Qi, of civilian registration in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jingming; he ranked thirteenth in family birth order and was aged forty-one [?; the transcription here reads 十三五四十一], born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Junjie, a commissioner (dashi); his grandfather was Daju; his father was Wencheng; and his mother was née Fu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Gang, and his younger brothers were Jing and Chun. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Xiao. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shou Ru, originally from Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, held civilian registration in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. He was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zonglu; he ranked second in family birth order and was aged twenty-five, born on the fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Chunling; his grandfather was An, a provincial graduate granted the cap and girdle of official status; his father was Zhang, a Study Companion; and his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Li, and his younger brothers were Lin and Feng. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventy-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ruli, originally from Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, held military registration in the Ningxia Guard, Shaanxi. He was a military student at the guard school, specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Liangbi; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged twenty, born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shizhen; his grandfather was Xiong; his father was Lian; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Ruji, Rulin, Ruming, and Ruyi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Kui, of military registration in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bocheng; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanlu; his grandfather was Eju; his father was Zigang; and his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Huo. He married a woman née Kang. He placed forty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陶纘〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣，民籍，國子生，治《書經》，字述之，行二，年二十九，五月十三日生。〕曾祖士賢，祖誠，父恂，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄績，弟緒，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百三十五名。

楊潭〔貫直隸保定府新城縣人，錦衣衛官籍，順天府學生，治《書經》，字宗淵，行二，年三十三，八月二十五日生。〕曾祖雲〔贈錦衣衛百戶〕，祖王〔錦衣衛百戶〕，父能〔冠帶總旗〕，母宋氏。嚴侍下，兄濂，弟澤、溥，娶髙氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第一百六十六名。
translation_en:
Guan Jing, registered in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongzhao, and he ranked fourteenth in his family. He was aged forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dejun, his grandfather Yingzhang, and his father Lingshao; his mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Cai. His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brothers were Dan, Yu, and Bing, and his younger brothers Xian 暹, Xian 顯, and Yi. He married a woman née Wu. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jingqi, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingliang, and he ranked twenty-fifth in his family. He was aged twenty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bi; his grandfather Yunhui was granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs. His father Yihong was Left Administration Assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Dong, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his stepmother, née Yuan, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brothers were Jingyong, Jingming, a tribute scholar, and Jinglong, an honorary official; his younger brothers were Jingdan and Jingyao. He married a woman née Tang. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Zuan, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shuzhi, and he ranked second in his family. He was aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian, his grandfather Cheng, and his father Xun; his mother was née Yang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ji and his younger brother Xu. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Tan was a native of Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, and a student of the Shuntian prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zongyuan, and he ranked second in his family. He was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yun was posthumously granted the title of Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his grandfather Wang was a Battalion Commander in that guard. His father Neng was a Company Commander granted the cap and girdle of official status; his mother was née Song. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Lian and his younger brothers Ze and Pu. He married a woman née Gao. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.
