translation_en:
Zeng Quan 曾全, registered in a military household in Yongxing County, Chenzhou, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Fuchu, he ranked third in his family, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rubai; his grandfather, Keqian, was posthumously granted the titles of Gentleman for Rendering Virtuous Service and Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Sui 䡵, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Chu, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tong, Jie, and Xiang, and his younger brothers were Qian and Nian; he married a woman née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Jian 徐鍵, registered in an officer household of the Jianning Left Guard, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Qizhi, he ranked first in his family, and he was forty years old, born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yi, was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather was Kan, his father was You, and his mother was née Luo. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Gang and Kuang; he married a woman née Zou and subsequently a woman née Tong. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tang 李堂, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shisheng, he ranked twelfth in his family, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taiheng, his grandfather was Boru, and his father was Ding; his father's former wife was née He, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yi, Jie, Qi, and Lin, the last a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brother was Chang. He married a woman née Yang and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Lin. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Luan 李鸞, registered in a military household in Gu'an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Tianrui, he ranked first in his family, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixing, his grandfather was Zhong, and his father, Rong, was formerly a Granary Vice Commissioner; his mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Hou. His father alone was living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 133rd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周旋〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字克敬，行五，年三十八，八月二十六日生〕。曾祖守行，祖世莊，父通，母王氏。慈侍下，兄曜，娶林氏。浙江鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百十七名。

汪鉉〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治《禮記》，字鼎卿，行四，年四十五，十月初十日生〕。曾祖彌彬，祖悠久〔知縣〕，父公遜，母吳氏。永感下，弟德卿、附卿、肅卿、用卿，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第五十三名，會試第五十三名。

毛珵〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字貞甫，行三，年三十六，七月十八日生〕。曾祖顯卿，祖以義，父僎，前母俞氏，母何氏。永感下，兄玉，弟瓚，娶韓氏。應天府鄉試第七十九名，會試第十二名。

萬祥〔貫廣西梧州府藤縣，軍籍，國子生，治《書經》，字世和，行五，年四十，六月初二日生〕。曾祖宗銘，祖伯齡〔大使〕，父子信，嫡母唐氏、張氏，生母陳氏。慈侍下，兄杲、顯，弟相、禎，娶蘇氏，繼娶唐氏。廣西鄉試第五十二名，會試第三百十三名。
translation_en:
Zhou Xuan, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kejing. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouxing, his grandfather Shizhuang, and his father Tong; his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Yao, and his wife was née Lin. He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Dingqing. Fourth in birth order, he was aged forty-five and was born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mibin, his grandfather Youjiu, a District Magistrate, and his father Gongxun; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Deqing, Fuqing, Suqing, and Yongqing, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-third in both the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Cheng, registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhenfu. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianqing, his grandfather Yiyi, and his father Zhuan; his father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yu and his younger brother Zan; his wife was née Han. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Xiang, registered in Teng County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shihe. Fifth in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongming, his grandfather Boling, a Commissioner, and his father Zixin; his legal mothers were née Tang and née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Chen. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Gao and Xian, and his younger brothers Xiang and Zhen. His wife was née Su; he subsequently married a woman née Tang. He placed fifty-second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡悳〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字允備，行十九，年二十九，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖祥〔封監察御史〕，祖敬〔贈按察司僉事〕，父謐〔布政司右參議〕，母章氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄福〔國子生〕、懌、恕、忱、恩〔貢士〕、恤〔聽選官〕、怡〔義官〕、愁、懋，弟栻、慥、愛、怟、應。娶章氏。浙江鄉試第二十五名，會試第八十四名。

匡翼之〔貫直隸淮安府贛榆縣，山東滕州千戶所官籍，國子生，治詩經，字斂敷，行二，年三十二，八月十四日生〕。曾祖德〔正千戶〕，祖濟〔千戶〕，父茂，前母婁氏，母郭氏。具慶下，兄直之，弟振之。娶綦氏。山東鄉試第七十一名，會試第二百四名。

許淳〔貫四川成都左護衛官籍，國子生，治易經，字文厚，行一，年三十六，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖榮，祖誠，父琛，母湯氏，繼母沈氏。重慶下，弟治、洪、溢、濂、澈、澍。娶郝氏。四川鄉試第二名，會試第二百十名。

謝汝暘〔貫湖廣衡州府衡陽縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字晉卿，行一，年三十一，正月十四日生〕。曾祖榮〔贈太常寺卿兼司經局正字〕，祖俊〔贈太常寺卿兼司經局正字〕，父宇〔太常寺卿兼司經局正字〕，母李氏〔贈淑人〕，繼母陸氏〔封淑人〕。具慶下，弟汝昭〔義官〕、汝明〔中書舍人〕、汝昌、汝昡。娶葛氏。湖廣鄉試第七十四名，會試第一百九名。
translation_en:
Hu De 胡悳, registered in a military household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yunbei. Nineteenth in family order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Xiang received the honorary appointment of Investigating Censor; his grandfather Jing was posthumously appointed Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father Mi was Right Assistant Administration Commissioner. His mother, née Zhang, received the title Yiren. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fu, a National University student; Yi; Shu; Chen; En, a tribute scholar; Xu, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Yi, an honorary official; Chou; and Mao. His younger brothers were Shi, Zao, Ai, Di, and Ying. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kuang Yizhi 匡翼之 was a native of Ganyu County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, with hereditary military-officer registration in the Tengzhou Battalion, Shandong. A National University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Lianfu. Second in family order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather De was a full Battalion Commander; his grandfather Ji was a Battalion Commander; and his father was Mao. His father’s former wife was née Lou, and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhizhi, and his younger brother was Zhenzhi. He married a woman née Qi. He ranked seventy-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chun 許淳 had hereditary military-officer registration in the Chengdu Left Escort Guard, Sichuan. A National University student, he specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenhou. First in family order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Cheng; and his father was Chen. His mother was née Tang, and his stepmother was née Shen. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhi, Hong, Yi, Lian, Che, and Shu. He married a woman née Hao. He ranked second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Ruyang 謝汝暘, registered in a military household in Hengyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jinqing. First in family order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Rong and grandfather Jun were each posthumously appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Orthographer in the Classics Documentation Office. His father Yu held those same offices. His mother, née Li, was posthumously granted the title Shuren; his stepmother, née Lu, received the same title. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruzhao, an honorary official; Ruming, a Secretariat Drafter; Ruchang; and Ruxuan. He married a woman née Ge. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Peng Jing, courtesy name Shuda, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiming, his grandfather Mengsi, his father Zhongying, and his mother née Weng; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Tai, Kun, and Sheng; his wife was née Chen; he ranked seventy-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yun, courtesy name Ruli, was registered in a commoner household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Xiao, his father Xuan, and his mother née Li; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Ying〔tribute scholar〕, Jian, and Mou; his wife was née Ru; he ranked 132nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Xue, courtesy name Wenjian, was registered in an official household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture; a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun’an, his grandfather Zhonghe, his father Xun, and his mother née Shen; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Xu, Ji, Yue, Xuan〔Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue〕, Chuo, Zuan, Hong〔tribute scholar〕, and Jin, and his younger brothers were Zi, Hou, Xiao, Xiang, Bo, Xiao (斅), and Ru; his wife was née Wang; he ranked eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Yi, courtesy name Zonglu, was registered in a military household in Xiangyin County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yingrui, his grandfather Qian〔Police Chief〕, his father Jun〔official awaiting selection for appointment〕, and his mother née Gan; both parents were living; his elder brother was Peng, and his younger brothers were Xi and Ji; his wife was née Xu; he ranked seventeenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Shen, registered in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Peizhi, and he ranked sixth in family birth order. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongcai; his grandfather, Qing, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his father, You, was an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun, and Jin, and his younger brothers were Gang and Ji. He married a woman née Lu. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zhu, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Mingyuan, and he ranked second in family birth order. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sijun; his grandfather was Ziyan; his father, Zong, was a Registrar; and his mother was née Jin. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brother was Rong. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Ang, registered in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guangbiao, and he ranked seventh in family birth order. He was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongzhan; his grandfather, Xuezhong, was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father, Xiang, was an Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Zhou, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xi, Lie, and Min, and his younger brother was Sheng. He married a woman née Deng. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Wan, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Quanqing, and he ranked first in family birth order. He was thirty years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shoudao; his grandfather was Heng; his father was Pu; and his mother was née Hua. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Xuan and Yu. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Hua. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dai En, registered in a medical household in Qianshan County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianxi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Juezong, his grandfather Wengong, and his father Mian, a Medical Officer (zhengke) in a medical school. His father's principal wife was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Shi. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Rong, and his wife was née Hu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chen, registered in a military household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xikui; he was aged thirty-five and born on the tenth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Kai; his grandfather Yong received the honorary title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father Fudeng was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Cheng, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren), and his stepmother, née Wang, was granted the same title. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Hou. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yu. He ranked seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Run, registered in a military household in Tai'an Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziwen; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Delu, his grandfather Xin, and his father Xi, a student of the Imperial University; his mother was née Wang. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuan, Hong, and Ze, and his younger brother was Lan. His wife was née Wang. He ranked sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third class: 238 men, granted the status of associate metropolitan graduate (tong jinshi chushen).

Ma Jingchang, registered in a civilian household in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tingyan; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Zhen (貞), his father Heng, and his mother née Yao. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Ang, Sheng (an honorary official), Zhao, and Yu (an honorary official); his younger brother was Jingxian. He was betrothed to a woman née Yao. He placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lin, registered in a civilian household in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingxiang; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-four years old, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wuzhong, his grandfather Shitai, his father Xizhi, and his mother née Gan. Both parents were still living. His younger brothers were Luan, Long, and Biao. He married a woman née Liao. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 333rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Zheng, registered in a civilian household in Qing County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongmin; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Mingyuan (posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Service), his grandfather Fushan, his father Neng (a County Magistrate), and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were still living. His younger brother was Jiu. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed forty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

吉人〔貫陝西西安府長安縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字惟正，行五，年三十六，五月二十三日生〕。曾祖元善，祖𨌆〔贈府同知〕，父慶〔大僕寺少卿〕，母蕭氏〔贈恭人〕，繼母胡氏。具慶下，兄亨、玄、臣〔縣丞〕、清，弟士傑、象占、芳、時卜，娶李氏。陝西鄉試第七名，會試第五十六名。

translation_en:
Liu Huai, of civilian registration in Luoshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dongzhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yuansi, his grandfather Xian, and his father Yi, a subprefect; his mother was née Ao and his stepmother née Jia. His father was living, and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Run, an honorary official, and Yong; his younger brother was Jun. His wife was née He. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Dezhi was a native of Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, with official registration in the Chong [?] Battalion of the Ningxia Central Guard, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Xizeng, ranked third among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shou, a company commander; his grandfather was Wang; and his father was Xuan, a company commander. His father's principal wife was née Xiao, and his birth mother was née Xu. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, a company commander, and Zhe. His wife was née Mou. He placed fifty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Ren, of military registration in Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Weizheng; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanshan; his grandfather was 𨌆 [reading uncertain], posthumously appointed associate prefect; and his father was Qing, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His mother, née Xiao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect; his stepmother was née Hu. His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brothers were Heng, Xuan, Chen, a county vice magistrate, and Qing; his younger brothers were Shijie, Xiangzhan, Fang, and Shibu [name divisions uncertain]. His wife was née Li. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Ding, of military registration in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Guoqi; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Huan, and his father Qian; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sheng and Huan. His wife was née Cai. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Liang, registered in a military household in Ningyuan County, Daozhou, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhichen; he ranked second among his brothers, was forty-three years old, and was born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dexian, his grandfather Xintong, his father Jizhou, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Ming was a Gentleman for Rendering Service; his younger brother was Peng. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed 132nd in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Lin, registered in a military household in Lin’an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a soldier of the Zhongyi Left Guard and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dezhang; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Li, his father Hong, and his mother née Zhong. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Xiao, Jin, and Xuan; his younger brothers were Zhang and Gui. He married a woman née Pan. He placed 131st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Hong, a native of Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, was registered in an officer household of the Daning Front Guard and was a student of the capital guards’ military school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bingde; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Qin was a Company Commander; his grandfather was Zheng; his father Xin was a Battalion Commander. His father’s earlier wife was née Tian, his mother née He, and his stepmother née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cong, a regular Battalion Commander, Lin, Yong, An, and Ning. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed 32nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wei, registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingwen; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather He was posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; his father Yu was an Administrative Assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Jing, an honorary official, Shen, Shou, and Shao, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Qi, Xiu, Ji, Xun, He, and Zhu. He married a woman née Qiu. He placed 33rd in the Henan Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Ao 袁翺, courtesy name Fengyi, was registered in a military household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizong; his grandfather, Jie; his father, Hong; his mother, née Dong; and his stepmother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xiang, Xu, and Yi, and his wife was née Li. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fu 彭敷, courtesy name Ruyan, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged fifty, born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather, Ling; his father, Wei; and his mother, née Lu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Qi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Zan 沈瓚, courtesy name Junxi, was a native of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonghua; his grandfather, Mingli; his father, Yinzhi; and his mother, née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yin, Zhen, Yu, and Cheng, and his wife was née Jin. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lan Ying 藍應, courtesy name Jingxiang, was registered in a military household of Xinghua Guard, Fujian. A student of the Xinghua Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyou; his grandfather, Yuanzhen; his father, Hongshao; his mother, née Li; and his stepmother, née Zhan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cheng, Bi, Fen, and Zhen; his younger brothers were Song, Xuan, Heng, Chen, and Geng; and his wife was née Hong. He placed seventy-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Ang 魯昂, courtesy name Tingzhan, was a native of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in an artisan household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junji, his grandfather Wende, and his father Zhongquan; his mother was née Ping. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Shen. He placed thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Liangcai 周亮采, courtesy name Bingchen, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhongli received the honorary title of Secretariat Drafter; his grandfather Xuan was a Secretariat Drafter; and his father Hao was a Secretariat Drafter, posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial. His mother, née Ling, received the title of Senior Lady of Peace. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Hang; his younger brothers were Hui and Chou, the latter a Recorder in the Court of State Ceremonial. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Duo 蔡鐸, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Wenshan was an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Yongyi, his father Lin, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qin, Ming, Yue, Yong, and Quan. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed sixty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zhao 鄭炤, courtesy name Shuzhao, was registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bojing, his grandfather Hou, and his father Xuan; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Fang. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jia Qin, registered in Lushan County, Ruzhou, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jingzhi, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Cheng was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Quan, and his father was Zhong. His mother and stepmother were both née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuan and Yong, and his wife was née Wei. He placed seventieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yuzhong, registered in Ziyang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Rongzheng, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-one years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiwang, his grandfather was Yu, and his father was Wenshi; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dazhong, and his younger brothers were Jiezhong and Xiezhong. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jin, registered in Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingyi, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Qing was an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang; his grandfather was Ning, and his father Wenji was a Timekeeper of the Five Offices. His mother was née Yuan. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Shen and Si. His wife was née Mao; his subsequent wife was née Wang. He placed 104th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yanghao, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Shimeng, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather was Xiang, and his father was Ning; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Xian, Da, Jun, Ying, Yi, Yangmeng, and Yangzheng [the division of the first five names is uncertain]; his younger brothers were Yanghui and Yangsu. His wife was née Tang. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ren Han, registered in Wenjiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zonghai. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Bitong, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Yongqin; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Pu, and his younger brothers were Yuan and Si. He married a woman née Zou. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Rui, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Fengyi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chuting, his grandfather Sicong, and his father Chun, a Prefect; his mother and stepmother were both née Wu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Gui, Fan, Yu, Xuan, Chen, Qi, and Ke. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jun, registered in Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanzhi. Third in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yiqing, a District Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his grandfather was Hu, Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his father was Dan, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Han, and his younger brothers were Run, Hao, Shu, and Pin. He married a woman née Ye and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Han, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruda. Eighth in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Wei, and his father Rui, an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his mother was née Lin. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Ze, Lian, and Hong. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Han You, registered in Jiaocheng County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianxi; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiliang, a Registrar; his grandfather was Yi; and his father was Yong, an Instructor. His father's principal wife was Lady Wang, and his birth mother was Lady Song. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xiang, an Instructor, and his wife was Lady Tan. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 336th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Changfan, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shiyin; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weizhi, his grandfather Jizhang, his father Mengchang, and his mother Lady Xu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Changquan and Changxi; his younger brothers were Jie and Changrong. His wife was Lady Wu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhen, a native of Gaoyi County, Zhao Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was registered in a banner household of the Guangning Central Garrison Guard in Liaodong. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiangru; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-seven years old, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Rong, and his father Jian, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under the applicable regulations. His mother was Lady Hou, and his stepmother was Lady Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lian, a Company Commander, Zan, and Fan; his wife was Lady Cheng. He placed 105th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 350th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Zhang, registered in Zhuo Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a military guard household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Lifang; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the thirtieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shineng, his grandfather Ping, and his father Cheng, a Clerk. His mother was Lady Xiao, and his stepmother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wan, and his wife was Lady Li. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Benshi, registered in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Chengzhi. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youfu, his grandfather Shengying, and his father Fu; his mother was née Ran. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Luo. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wenying, registered in Xiping County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jinghua. He was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youcai, his grandfather Ning, and his father Zhong; his mother was née Dong. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chun, registered in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zonghou. He was tenth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhentong, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Yu, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father was Jian, a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qing, Hao, and Shen, and his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Li. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ji, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Daji. He was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanli, his grandfather Jing, and his father Hai, an Assistant Salt Distribution Commissioner; his mother was née Yu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jing, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Lun, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; and Gang. He married a woman née Sun. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 348th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Tai, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zitong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zaier, his grandfather Zhigao, and his father Chaoqi; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yong, and his wife was née Lin. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Ji, registered in a commandant household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yishi, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Boyao, his grandfather Digang, and his father Duo; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Han, his younger brothers were Pu, Wei, Chao, and Run, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shiliang, registered in a military household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Chongzhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Taisheng, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Yuantao, and his father Mei; his mother was née Dong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Shifang, his younger brothers were Shichang, Shifu, Shibi, and Shibao, and his wife was née Tao. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Yinxian, originally from Yizhang County, Chenzhou, Huguang, and registered in a civilian household in Chang'an County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shide, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the intercalary second month. His great-grandfather was Fashou, his grandfather Liangjie, and his father Long, Vice Magistrate of a Department; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rukun, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fourteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

戴初〔貫直隸廣德州建平縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字復之，行五，年三十九，六月初九日生〕。曾祖元卿，祖寧，父輝，母宋氏。慈侍下，兄暹，娶史氏。應天府鄉試第五十五名，會試第八十六名。

黃世經〔貫陝西秦州衛，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字時濟，行一，年三十一，四月初五日生〕。曾祖得才，祖秀，父凱〔監生〕，母張氏。具慶下，弟世綸、世維，娶雷氏。陝西鄉試第二十一名，會試第二百五十名。

張掖〔貫陝西鳳翔府鳳翔縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字輔之，行二，年四十一，六月二十八日生〕。曾祖義，祖玉〔教諭〕，父守樂〔巡檢〕，嫡母高氏，繼母秦氏，生母閻氏。慈侍下，兄拯〔監生〕，弟援、掄、授，娶石氏，繼娶楊氏。陝西鄉試第十名，會試第九十九名。

文森〔貫湖廣衡州府衡山縣人，直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字宗嚴，行三，年二十六，四月十三日生〕。曾祖定聡，祖惠，父洪〔教諭，贈太僕寺寺丞〕，前母陳氏〔贈安人〕，母顧氏〔贈安人〕，繼母吕氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄倫〔千戶〕、林〔太僕寺寺丞〕，弟彬，娶談氏。應天府鄉試第三十二名，會試第六十七名。
translation_en:
Dai Chu, courtesy name Fuzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jianping County, Guangde Subprefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanqing; his grandfather, Ning; his father, Hui; and his mother, née Song. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Xian, and his wife was née Shi. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Shijing, courtesy name Shiji, was registered in a military household of Qinzhou Guard, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Decai; his grandfather, Xiu; his father, Kai, an Imperial University student; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shilun and Shiwei, and his wife was née Lei. He ranked twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ye, courtesy name Fuzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Yu, a School Instructor; and his father, Shoule, a Police Chief. His father's principal wife was née Gao, his stepmother was née Qin, and his birth mother was née Yan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Zheng, an Imperial University student, and his younger brothers were Yuan, Lun, and Shou. He married a woman née Shi and subsequently a woman née Yang. He ranked tenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Sen, courtesy name Zongyan, was a native of Hengshan County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dingcong; his grandfather, Hui; and his father, Hong, a School Instructor posthumously granted the title of Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud. His father's former wife, née Chen, and his mother, née Gu, were each posthumously granted the title of Lady of Tranquility; his stepmother, née Lü, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Lun, a Battalion Commander, and Lin, an Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud; his younger brother was Bin. His wife was née Tan. He ranked thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

虞坤〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字公載，行二，年三十四，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖忠，祖韶，父廷〔教諭〕，嫡母劉氏，生母郝氏。重慶下，兄乾，娶徐氏。江西鄉試第九十五名，會試第一百五名。

蔣昪〔貫湖廣永州府祁陽縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字寅暘，行一，年三十，閏二月二十日生〕。曾祖貴卿，祖富一，父亮〔府通判〕，母曾氏，繼母呂氏。具慶下，弟冕、昂、昪、暹、昇、晟、昺、春、昕、暴，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第三十一名，會試第三十六名。

白翺〔貫四川成都府綿州人，府軍前衛軍籍，國子生，治書經，字鳳儀，行二，年二十六，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖敏受，祖聰〔遇例冠帶〕，父永通〔冠帶將軍〕，母陳氏。重慶下，兄昂，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第三十四名，會試第一百九十六名。

吳廷舉〔貫廣西梧州守禦千戶所，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字獻臣，行一，年二十六，九月初十日生〕。曾祖源富，祖貴宗，父英，母駱氏。永感下，弟廷弼、廷諤、廷諫、廷議、廷諮、廷讓，娶馮氏。廣西鄉試第十七名，會試第一百三十三名。
translation_en:
Yu Kun 虞坤, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Gongzai, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Shao, and his father Ting, an Instructor; his father's principal wife was née Liu and his birth mother née Hao. His grandparents and parents were living; his elder brother was Qian, and his wife was née Xu. He ranked ninety-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Bian 蔣昪, registered in Qiyang County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yinyang, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twentieth day of the intercalary second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guiqing, his grandfather Fuyi, and his father Liang, an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Zeng and his stepmother née Lü. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Mian, Ang, Bian [?, repeating his own given name], Xian, Sheng, Sheng, Bing, Chun, Xin, and Bao, and his wife was née Liu. He ranked thirty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Ao 白翺, a native of Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a military household of the Vanguard Guard of the Imperial Guard and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Fengyi, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minshou, his grandfather Cong, who had been granted the right to wear an official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations, and his father Yongtong, a general entitled to wear an official cap and girdle; his mother was née Chen. His grandparents and parents were living; his elder brother was Ang, and his wife was née Li. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Tingju 吳廷舉, registered in a military household of the Wuzhou Defensive Battalion, Guangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xianchen, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanfu, his grandfather Guizong, and his father Ying; his mother was née Luo. Both parents were deceased; his younger brothers were Tingbi, Ting'e, Tingjian, Tingyi, Tingzi, and Tingrang, and his wife was née Feng. He ranked seventeenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

柴昇〔貫河南南陽府鄧州內鄉縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字公照，行一，年三十二，十一月初九日生〕。曾祖恭，祖蘭〔判官〕，父文璋，母蘇氏。具慶下，弟旻、昂，娶曲氏。河南鄉試第十九名，會試第一百十名。

朱綬〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字文佩，行二，年四十，正月初三日生〕。曾祖彥昭，祖常，父璠〔工副〕，母伍氏。具慶下，兄紱，娶胡氏，繼娶吳氏、王氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第二百四十五名。
translation_en:
Xu [?] (許𤐣), courtesy name Jinghui, was from Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bo’an; his grandfather, Shou; and his father, Yi, a Judge. His mother was née Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xin, and his younger brother was Jianshi. He married a woman née Ye. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Han (李瀚), courtesy name Wenbo, was from Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congyi; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Zhong, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ze, Yuan, and Wei [?]. He married a woman née Hao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Sheng (柴昇), courtesy name Gongzhao, was from Neixiang County, Dengzhou Subprefecture, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather, Lan, an Administrative Assistant; and his father, Wenzhang. His mother was née Su. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Min and Ang. He married a woman née Qu. He placed nineteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shou (朱綬), courtesy name Wenpei, was from Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged forty, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhao; his grandfather, Chang; and his father, Fan, a Vice Director of Works [?]. His mother was née Wu (伍). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently women née Wu (吳) and Wang. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ouyang Peng 歐陽鵬, courtesy name Shiju, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in family birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guanmin, his grandfather Yongren, and his father Guangjun; his mother was née Kang and his stepmother née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Ning was an Admonisher in the household of the Prince of Lu; his younger brothers were E, Feng, Hong, and Ying. He married a woman née Liang. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Fu 伍符, courtesy name Chaoxin, was registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in family birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Mian was a County Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather Tixiang had previously been granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father Xiyuan was a Prefect, and his mother, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Chou, Jian, Ce, Fan, Zhuan, Zhen, and Ji. He married a woman née Ouyang. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Shi 毛詩, courtesy name Dajing, was registered in Ye County, Yuzhou Subprefecture, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he was fifth in family birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Gang, and his father Xuan; his mother was née Pian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tong, a School Instructor, Ben, and Zong; his younger brother was Sui. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Fan. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Kuan 童寬, courtesy name Jizhi, was registered in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was seventh in family birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhongying was a Registrar; his grandfather was Tingyan and his father Yuan’an; his mother was née Shi. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Ying, Xi, Jing, and Jia; his younger brothers were Kang, Xiu, Kan, and Huan. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Weng Jianzhi, courtesy name Yingqian, was from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the tenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Ci, was granted the title of Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Di, was a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Xiong, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shunzhi and Yingqian. He married a woman née Pan. He ranked third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xunxue, courtesy name Xixian, was from Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to an artisan household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Mingdao; and his father, Jun, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Duan and his stepmother née Lu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Xunzhi. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked seventy-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Fu, courtesy name Liangchen, was from Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bisheng; his grandfather, Tianxiang; and his father, Yanzhong, a sacrificial attendant (shengji guan). His mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Cao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bi, Zuo, You, and Qing. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently a woman née Xue. He ranked forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Jie, courtesy name Xiufu, was registered with Zhuolu Left Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and belonged to a military household. A student of the Zhuozhou Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Xian; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Feng and Shen, and his younger brothers were Lun and Ru. He married a woman née Tong. He ranked one hundred twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Deng Yi 鄧頥, courtesy name Xingzheng, was from Luzhou, Sichuan, and registered in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shengzu; his grandfather, Chen Bin [?]; his father, Jun, was granted the title of Secretary; and his mother, née Yang, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother, Shun, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his younger brother was Yan. He married a woman née Xian. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fu 張黼, courtesy name Shiqin, was from Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Mingfu, was a Director of a County School; his grandfather was Shu; his father, Shao, was a National University student granted the cap and girdle of official status; and his mother was née Sheng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Fu 黻. He married a woman née Yin and subsequently a woman née Qu. He placed forty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang En 王恩, courtesy name Kecheng, was from Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a military salt-producing household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was twentieth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Guixue; his grandfather, Shiyi; and his father, Min. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Yu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yan, Shen, Qi, and Yi; his younger brother was Tong. He married a woman née Xu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Zhi 鄒智, courtesy name Ruyu, was from Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yingzong; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Taichang; and his mother, née Feng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Chi and Xin. He married a woman née Liu. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Xun, of Yongchuan County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Qingji, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiliang, a tribute student; his grandfather was Jie; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jia, Mo, Xi, and Dian, and his wife was née Cheng. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu E, of Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Liangju, he ranked ninth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Shenzhi; his father was Guan; and his mother was née Ge. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Peng and Kun, and his wife was née Gao. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kui, registered with Yingchuan Guard under the Henan Regional Military Commission, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Chaoyang, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather was Gui; his father was Cong, an honorary official; and his mother was née Yan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Lan, and his wife was née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Zhen, of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuanshan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Yu; his father was Yong; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zuo, an honorary official, and his wife was née Liu. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 321st in the Metropolitan Examination.

方天然〔貫直隸揚州衛官籍，國子生，治詩經，字希誠，行三，年三十八，五月十六日生〕。曾祖原正，祖玉，父祚，嫡母呂氏，生母印氏。慈侍下，兄天祥、天瑞，弟天奇、天倫、天叙、天秩，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第九十三名，會試第二百二十六名。

張嵿〔貫浙江紹興府蕭山縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字時峻，行四，年三十，七月初八日生〕。曾祖仕寧，祖清，父孔殷，母俞氏。具慶下，兄山、巖，弟嶔，娶戴氏。浙江鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百三十七名。

羅政〔貫江西臨江府新喻縣軍籍，縣學生，治春秋，字皆正，行十七，年二十八，二月初十日生〕。曾祖孟俊，祖時堅，父端鵬，母楊氏。嚴侍下，兄皆元、皆會、皆序、皆貞，弟皆明，娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百六十名。

邢纓〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄州黃梅縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字文甫，行一，年三十五，十一月十五日生〕。曾祖德茂，祖仕聰，父暹，母周氏。慈侍下，弟綬、緌、綱，娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百三十六名。
translation_en:
Fang Tianran, registered in an official household of Yangzhou Guard in Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xicheng; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanzheng, his grandfather Yu, and his father Zuo; his father's principal wife was Lady Lü, and his birth mother was Lady Yin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Tianxiang and Tianrui; his younger brothers were Tianqi, Tianlun, Tianxu, and Tianzhi. He married Lady Liu. He placed ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ding, registered in a civilian household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shijun; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty, born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shining, his grandfather Qing, his father Kongyin, and his mother Lady Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan and Yan, and his younger brother was Qin. He married Lady Dai. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Zheng, registered in a military household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jiezheng; he ranked seventeenth in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Mengjun, his grandfather Shijian, his father Duanpeng, and his mother Lady Yang. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Jieyuan, Jiehui, Jiexu, and Jiezhen; his younger brother was Jieming. He married Lady Xiao. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Ying, registered in a military household in Huangmei County, Qizhou Subprefecture, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Wenfu; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Demao, his grandfather Shicong, his father Xian, and his mother Lady Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shou, Rui, and Gang. He married Lady Li. He placed thirty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周鉞〔貫四川夔州府梁山縣人，陝西西安左衛軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字廷儀，行二，年二十七，四月二十四日生〕。曾祖均美，祖成，父信〔知縣〕，母陳氏。具慶下，兄鑑〔義官〕，娶曹氏。陝西鄉試第三十七名，會試第八十九名。

translation_en:
Li Pu, registered in Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zongda; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinzhong; his grandfather, Rong; and his father, Yan, a subprefectural Clerk. His mother was née Bian, and his stepmother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan, Hu, a District Magistrate, and Shu. He married a woman née Ma. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yue, a native of Liangshan County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a military household of the Xi’an Left Guard in Shaanxi. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tingyi; he ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junmei; his grandfather, Cheng; and his father, Xin, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother Jian held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness. He married a woman née Cao. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Duo, a native of Bao’an County, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was registered in a military household of the Minzhou Guard. He was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Dazhen; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather, Liang; and his father, Yu. His mother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Rui, Xuan, and Pu. He married a woman née Bai. He placed fiftieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Fu, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Kongxiu; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongqi; his grandfather, Yin; and his father, Min. His mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jie, Pei, and Fu, and his younger brother was Ying. He married a woman née Xie. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiang Shi 向時, registered in a military household in Yuechi County, Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weizhong, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Youmin, his grandfather Faqing, his father Quan, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living, his wife was née Lei, and he ranked forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji 王濟, a native of Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a military household of Hejian Guard and was a student of the Hejian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongji, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Da, his grandfather Xian, and his father Neng, a County Magistrate; his father’s former wife was née Li and his mother née Yan; he had living grandparents and parents, his younger brother was Ze, his wife was née Li, and he ranked fifty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Bao 石珤, registered in a civilian household in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the County School specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bangyan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Youzhi, his grandfather Lin, granted the honorary title of Examining Editor, his father Yu, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and his mother née Zhao, granted the title of Lady (ruren); both parents were living, his elder brother Jie was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, his younger brother was Xu, his wife was née Wang, and he ranked third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zongzai 鄭宗載, registered in a military household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a County School student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Benhou, he was first in birth order, and he was aged forty, born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xianggong, his grandfather Ji, his father Xiqi, his mother née Xiao, and his stepmother née Cai; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Zonghan and Zongxiao, his wife was née Jiang, and he ranked thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.
