punctuated:
榮節〔貫河南汝寧府遂平縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字應中，行六，年三十一，七月十七日生〕。曾祖玉，祖整，父和，前母李氏，母張氏。具慶下，兄顯、逹、華、福、爵，弟祿、時、珮、逵，娶魏氏。河南鄉試第十八名，會試第五十九名。

張津〔貫廣東惠州府博羅縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字廣漢，行一，年二十六，正月二十三日生〕。曾祖德裕，祖衡，父鐸〔知縣〕，前母李氏，母黃氏。具慶下，弟渉、澍、澈、渥，娶曾氏。廣東鄉試第五十八名，會試第八十七名。

張瀾〔貫河南河南府新安縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字道本，行三，年四十二，二月初六日生〕。曾祖時中〔通判〕，祖宗玉〔縣丞〕，父鉞〔進士，州同知，贈戶部主事〕，母宰氏〔贈安人〕，繼母方氏。永感下，兄澍〔知府〕、瀚〔訓科〕，弟溥〔貢士〕，娶侯氏。河南鄉試第五十二名，會試第三百十八名。

張相〔貫四川順慶府蓬州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字佐虞，行二，年四十一，十一月二十三日生〕。曾祖友鵬，祖志虎，父郁〔寺丞〕，母髙氏。具慶下，兄廡，娶辛氏。四川鄉試第六十名，會試第三百名。
translation_en:
Rong Jie, courtesy name Yingzhong, was from Suiping County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Zheng, and his father He; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xian, Da, Hua, Fu, and Jue; his younger brothers were Lu, Shi, Pei, and Kui. He married a woman née Wei. He ranked eighteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jin, courtesy name Guanghan, was from Boluo County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and belonged to a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deyu, his grandfather Heng, and his father Duo, a District Magistrate; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were She, Shu, Che, and Wo. He married a woman née Zeng. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lan, courtesy name Daoben, was from Xin'an County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhong, an Assistant Prefect; his grandfather was Zongyu, a District Vice Magistrate; and his father was Yue, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) and Department Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Zai, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his stepmother was née Fang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shu, a Prefect, and Han, whose title is transcribed as xunke [?]; his younger brother was Pu, a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Hou. He ranked fifty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiang, courtesy name Zuoyu, was from Peng Department, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youpeng, his grandfather Zhihu, and his father Yu, an Assistant in a court; his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wu. He married a woman née Xin. He ranked sixtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zhen, courtesy name Yuanpin, was registered in Hezhou, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household. A student of the department school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Youcai, and his father Jing; his mother was née Dao [?]. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Jing, Qi, and Shan, and he married a woman née Tong. He ranked ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chongsi, courtesy name Shixiu, was registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in an official household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes, he was seventh in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Guan received the honorary title of Supervising Secretary; his grandfather Fan was Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; and his father Ji'an was a Prefectural School Instructor. His father's former wife was née Tian, and his mother was also née Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiasi, Zhaosi, Yuansi, Zhensi, Yisi, and Yansi; his younger brothers were Zongsi, Chengsi, and Xuansi. He was betrothed to a woman née Wu. He ranked eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Fu, courtesy name Shangchou, was registered in Daizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Liangzuo was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather was Jin; and his father Yongwei was a Station Master. His mother was née Gao. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Gou, Xi, Zhen, and Kai, and he married a woman née Wang. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Jiuling, courtesy name Shouqing, was registered in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Juyi, his grandfather Du, and his father Tinggui; his mother was née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiuding, Jiusi (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Jiucheng, and Jiuwan. He married a woman née Ding and subsequently married women née Shen and née Feng. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

石玠〔貫直隸真定府藁城縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字邦秀，行一，年二十五，八月初六日生〕。曾祖友智，祖麟〔教諭，贈御史〕，父玉〔按察司副使〕，母趙氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，弟珤〔同科進士〕、珝，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第三名，會試第二百三十五名。

倪天民〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣人，武功中衛軍匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字秀夫，行一，年三十六，四月十九日生〕。曾祖榮，祖覺清，父信，母曹氏。慈侍下，娶朱氏，繼娶紀氏。順天府鄉試第四名，會試第二十七名。

和鵬〔貫山西太原府平定州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字大舉，行四，年三十七，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖桂，祖揖，父良弼，母呂氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，兄鸞〔知府〕、鳳、鴻，娶楊氏。山西鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百三十五名。

范伸〔貫山東兗州府曲阜縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字邦直，行一，年四十三，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖羽〔百戶〕，祖禮〔百戶〕，父英，母張氏。具慶下，弟价，娶嚴氏。山東鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百九十二名。
translation_en:
Shi Jie, registered in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bangxiu. First in birth order, he was twenty-five years old and was born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzhi; his grandfather, Lin, was an Instructor posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father, Yu, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Zhao, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bao, a jinshi of the same examination cohort, and Xu. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Tianmin, a native of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered as a military artisan in the Wugong Central Guard and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xiufu. First in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Jueqing, his father Xin, and his mother a woman née Cao. His mother alone was living. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Ji. He ranked fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Peng, registered in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Daju. Fourth in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Yi, his father Liangbi, his mother a woman née Lü, and his stepmother a woman née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Luan, a Prefect, Feng, and Hong. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Shen, registered in Qufu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bangzhi. First in birth order, he was forty-three years old and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yu, and grandfather, Li, were both Company Commanders; his father was Ying, and his mother was a woman née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jie. He married a woman née Yan. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
杜啓〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子開，行二，年三十六，正月二十一日生〕。曾祖宗智，祖玉，父瓊，前母陸氏、張氏，母王氏。永感下，兄嗣昌，弟咨，娶顧氏。應天府鄉試第八十三名，會試第二十八名。

丁榮〔貫直隸安慶府懷寧縣，民匠籍，縣學生，治詩經，字宗仁，行一，年三十四，五月初七日生〕。曾祖禮，祖紹，父順，母楊氏。慈侍下，弟煥、燉、熖、煌、燦、焸、燧、熝、煪、熾、燔，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百五十八名。

唐希介〔貫山西太原府陽曲縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字景賢，行四，年三十四，正月十五日生〕。曾祖拳〔贈太僕寺寺丞〕，祖巍，父誠〔知縣〕，母王氏。永感下，兄質、斌、瑀，弟璠，娶李氏。山西鄉試第三名，會試第一百九十四名。

郎滋〔貫浙江嚴州府建德縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字德潤，行一，年三十二，七月二十八日生〕。曾祖與道，祖士原〔封御史〕，父勝〔按察司副使〕，嫡母孫氏〔封孺人〕，生母汪氏。具慶下，娶滕氏。浙江鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百四十九名。
translation_en:
Du Qi 杜啓, courtesy name Zikai, was from Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongzhi; his grandfather, Yu; and his father, Qiong. His father's former wives were née Lu and née Zhang, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Sichang, and his younger brother was Zi. His wife was née Gu. He placed eighty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Rong 丁榮, courtesy name Zongren, was from Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a civilian artisan household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Shao; his father, Shun; and his mother, née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Huan 煥, Dun 燉, Yan 熖, Huang 煌, Can 燦, Gu 焸 [?], Sui 燧, Lu 熝, Qiu 煪, Chi 熾, and Fan 燔. His wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Xijie 唐希介, courtesy name Jingxian, was from Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and belonged to a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, posthumously granted the title of Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his grandfather was Wei; his father was Cheng, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhi, Bin, and Yu, and his younger brother was Fan. His wife was née Li. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lang Zi 郎滋, courtesy name Derun, was from Jiande County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yudao; his grandfather was Shiyuan, granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Sheng, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His legal mother was née Sun, granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his birth mother was née Wang 汪. Both parents were living. His wife was née Teng. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
胡承〔貫直隸鎮海衛官籍，國子生，治易經，字安節，行一，年四十，七月十九日生〕。曾祖關〔百戶〕，祖通〔千戶〕，父庸，嫡母邵氏，生母陶氏。永感下，娶茅氏。應天府鄉試第九十一名，會試第二百九十八名。

王術〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字用仁，行五，年二十六，五月二十六日生〕。曾祖青，祖鑑，父洪，母羅氏。具慶下，兄彰〔省祭官〕、椿，弟祭、森、懋、梵，娶孫氏。浙江鄉試第七十六名，會試第九十二名。

俞世德〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字守宗，行一，年三十六，九月初六日生〕。曾祖文質，祖縉，父本〔大使〕，母楊氏。慈侍下，弟世美、世章、世則，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第十五名，會試第三百十名。

徐紹先〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄水縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字繼之，行一，年三十九，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖信中，祖友詳，父法〔除教授〕，母張氏。慈侍下，弟紹魁、紹元，娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第二十八名，會試第三百三名。
translation_en:
Hu Cheng, registered in an official household of Zhenhai Guard in Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Anjie; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Guan, a Company Commander; his grandfather was Tong, a Battalion Commander; and his father was Yong. His legal mother was née Shao, and his birth mother was née Tao. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Mao. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shu, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yongren; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Jian, his father Hong, and his mother née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang, a sacrificial official (shengji guan), and Chun; his younger brothers were Ji, Sen, Mao, and Fan. His wife was née Sun. He placed seventy-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shide, registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shouzong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi, his grandfather Jin, his father Ben, a Commissioner, and his mother née Yang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shimei, Shizhang, and Shize. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shaoxian, registered in a military household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jizhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xinzhong, his grandfather Youxiang, his father Fa, who was appointed a Prefectural School Instructor, and his mother née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shaokui and Shaoyuan. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Fu, registered in an official household in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Derao; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouyong, his grandfather Weixin, and his father Zongning; his mother was née Zhang. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Lu and Zhen, and his wife was née Li. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ce, registered in a guardsman's household in Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boxiang, his grandfather Liang, and his father Birong; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian, Zan, Jie, and Zhen, and his wife was née Huang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chao Jinxiao, registered in a military household in Gaoyang County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Keren; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian, his grandfather Rong, and his father Gang; his father's former wife was née Li, his mother née Zhai, and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Sheng and Yu, the latter a sacrificial attendant (shengjiguan); his younger brothers were Xianliang, Jinli, and Jinyi. His wife was née Li. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Liang, a native of Qihe County, Shandong, registered in an official household of the Shenwu Left Guard, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Suizhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jie and grandfather Zhen were both company commanders; his father was Rang, and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Zong. His wife was née Jin; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Zhen, registered in an officer household of Qingyang Guard under the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenjing, he was first in birth order, and he was aged forty, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Si, Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief; his grandfather was You, Vice Commander; his father was Fu, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Yu. He placed thirteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Jing, registered in a military household in Lan County, Kelan Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yizhi, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Mao, a Registrar; his grandfather was Zhirong, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Xuan, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Lu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Lun, Jin, Shen, Ji, and Xu, and his wife was née Wen. He placed thirteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Xingze County, Zhengzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tizhen, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Er, his grandfather was Neng, his father was Zhao, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hui, Yi, and Qing, and his wife was née Sun. He placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jian, registered in a civilian household in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Huizhi, he was second in birth order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Dashe, his grandfather was Zhen, his father was Jing, his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Duo, and his younger brothers were Xuan and Yu. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married women née Zheng and née Fu. He placed twenty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yong, registered in a military household in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shixian, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deming, his grandfather Qian, and his father Yi, a School Instructor; his mother was née Liu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Zan and Zhi, and his younger brother Jian; he married a woman née He. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhang, registered in a civilian household in Longqing Subprefecture, directly administered by the capital, was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Derun, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siwen, his grandfather Duo, and his father Qin; his father's former wife was née Wei, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Qi; he married a woman née Wang. He ranked forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Zundao, registered in a civilian household in Duchang County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yaochen, he was second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siben, his grandfather Yuanbo, and his father Yong; his mother was née Chen. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Zongdao, and his younger brothers Youdao and Hongdao; he married a woman née Wu. He ranked sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Hao, registered in a civilian household in Le'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jingji, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bobin, his grandfather Maozhao, and his father Houshan; his mother was née Deng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Shiya; he married a woman née Deng and subsequently a woman née Guan. He ranked thirty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
紀鏞〔貫直隸鳳陽府潁州太和縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字大器，行一，年四十一，七月十七日生〕。曾祖仲延，祖叔訥，父若思，母張氏。永感下，弟欽、釗，娶李氏。應天府鄉試第六十七名，會試第二百七十五名。

國瑀〔貫山東濟南府濱州軍籍，州學生，治春秋，字朝佩，行二，年二十六，二月二十七日生〕。曾祖彥臣，祖思賢，父文著，前母李氏，母王氏。慈侍下，兄寧，娶申氏。山東鄉試第四十五名，會試第三百三十四名。

秦渙〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字汝亨，行十四，年四十，二月初一日生〕。曾祖森，祖浩，父玒，母阮氏。永感下，兄濂、澄、源、潭、洊、澮、淮、淳、浤、瀚，弟洪，娶虞氏。浙江鄉試第七十四名，會試第八十名。

李𤉨〔貫四川夔州府東鄉縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字茂林，行二，年三十八，十二月二十日生〕。曾祖文富，祖彰〔巡檢〕，父敏〔教諭〕，前母程氏，母徐氏。永感下，兄棠，弟粟，娶蕭氏。四川鄉試第五十七名，會試第三百三十五名。
translation_en:
Ji Yong 紀鏞, courtesy name Daqi, was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Yingzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhongyan, his grandfather Shune, his father Ruosi, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were deceased, his younger brothers were Qin and Zhao, and his wife was née Li; he placed sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Yu 國瑀, courtesy name Chaopei, was registered in a military household in Binzhou Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong; he was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yanchen, his grandfather Sixian, his father Wenzhu, his father's former wife née Li, and his mother née Wang; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brother was Ning, and his wife was née Shen; he placed forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 334th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Huan 秦渙, courtesy name Ruheng, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked fourteenth among his brothers, and was aged forty, born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sen, his grandfather Hao, his father Hong, and his mother née Ruan; both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Lian, Cheng, Yuan, Tan, Jian, Hui, Huai, Chun, Hong 浤, and Han, his younger brother was Hong 洪, and his wife was née Yu; he placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lin [?] 李𤉨, courtesy name Maolin, was registered in a civilian household in Dongxiang County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wenfu, his grandfather Zhang 〔Police Chief〕, his father Min 〔Instructor〕, his father's former wife née Cheng, and his mother née Xu; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Tang, his younger brother Su, and his wife was née Xiao; he placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 335th in the Metropolitan Examination.

許鵬〔貫山東青州府樂安縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字圖南，行三，年三十三，四月初一日生〕。曾祖大綱，祖文質，父鑑，嫡母宋氏，生母王氏。具慶下，兄榮、積，娶宋氏。山東鄉試第二十五名，會試第三百二十七名。

蔡杲〔貫福建漳州府龍溪縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字特明，行二，年三十，九月初九日生〕。曾祖孔脩，祖邦禮，父宗苓，母林氏。慈侍下，兄塘，弟櫪、欄、桁，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第六十四名，會試第一百二十四名。

白鸞〔貫陝西鳳翔府寶雞縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字孟禽，行一，年三十，十月初一日生〕。曾祖和，祖昇，父信，母張氏。具慶下，弟鳳、鶴、鷺、鸑、鷟、鷗，娶賈氏。陝西鄉試第六十名，會試第二十五名。

陳端〔貫四川重慶府忠州墊江縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字廷表，行二，年三十九，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖珪，祖仲禮，父仕輔，母程氏。嚴侍下，兄彬，弟常，娶姜氏，繼娶周氏。四川鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百九十名。
translation_en:
Xu Peng, registered in Le’an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tunan, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dagang, his grandfather Wenzhi, and his father Jian; his father's principal wife was née Song and his birth mother née Wang; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Rong and Ji, his wife was née Song, and he placed twenty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 327th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Gao, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Teming, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongxiu, his grandfather Bangli, his father Zongling, and his mother née Lin; his mother alone was living, his elder brother was Tang and his younger brothers were Li, Lan, and Heng, his wife was née Zheng, and he placed sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Luan, registered in Baoji County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Mengqin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was He, his grandfather Sheng, his father Xin, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Feng, He, Lu, Yue, Zhuo, and Ou, his wife was née Jia, and he placed sixtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Duan, registered in Dianjiang County, Zhong Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingbiao, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Zhongli, his father Shifu, and his mother née Cheng; his father alone was living, his elder brother was Bin and his younger brother Chang, he married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Zhou, and he placed fifty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃玄齡〔貫江西南康府建昌縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字崇壽，行三，年四十三，四月十四日生〕。曾祖明哲，祖伯澄〔主簿〕，父大綸，母舒氏。具慶下，兄鶴齡、栢齡，弟九齡，娶胡氏。江西鄉試第九十五名，會試第一百二十五名。

葉清〔貫浙江紹興府蕭山縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字本澄，行二，年三十六，十月十四日生〕。曾祖茂實，祖擇善，父孟儔，母陸氏。慈侍下，兄昇，娶曹氏，繼娶朱氏。浙江鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百三十一名。

李璽〔貫江西建昌府南豐縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字德貴，行二，年三十五，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖尚文，祖宗賢〔遇例冠帶〕，父時清，母丁氏。具慶下，兄瑩，娶曽氏。江西鄉試第九名，會試第一百十二名。

趙文奎〔貫湖廣荊州府江陵縣，民籍，府學生，治書經，字天章，行二，年三十二，三月十六日生〕。曾祖繼貴，祖添禮，父安前，母張氏，母劉氏。具慶下，兄文英，弟文衡，娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第六十八名，會試第三百六名。
translation_en:
Huang Xuanling, courtesy name Chongshou, was from Jianchang County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a military household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, third in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingzhe; his grandfather was Bocheng, Registrar; his father was Dalun; and his mother was née Shu; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Heling and Bailing, his younger brother was Jiuling, and his wife was née Hu; he placed ninety-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Qing, courtesy name Bencheng, was from Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a civilian household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maoshi, his grandfather Zeshan, his father Mengchou, and his mother née Lu; his mother alone was living, his elder brother was Sheng, and he married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Zhu; he placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xi, courtesy name Degui, was from Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a military household; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangwen; his grandfather was Zongxian, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and belt under the applicable regulations; his father was Shiqing; and his mother was née Ding; both parents were living, his elder brother was Ying, and his wife was née Zeng; he placed ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Wenkui, courtesy name Tianzhang, was from Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, registered in a civilian household; he was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jigui, his grandfather Tianli, and his father Anqian; the entry lists a mother née Zhang and a mother née Liu, without distinguishing their status; both parents were living, his elder brother was Wenying, his younger brother Wenheng, and his wife was née Li; he placed sixty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周南〔貫四川成都府井研縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字化行，行五，年三十八，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖子富，祖毅〔貢士〕，父庸，前母陳氏，母李氏。具慶下，兄秉彛、秉和、秉誠、讓，弟麟、鳳，娶龍氏。四川鄉試第八名，會試第二百二十九名。

translation_en:
Zheng Hong 鄭弘, courtesy name Daoxi, was registered in a civilian household in Weinan County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi; he was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Suowan, his grandfather Li, his father Zhi, and his mother née Fan; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Jingchun, his younger brother Zhong, and his wife née Ren; he placed fifty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Hua 胡崋, courtesy name Weijun, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenhai, his grandfather Yangao, his father Qi, his legal mother née Chen, and his birth mother née Zhou; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Yue, Song, Gang, and Qin, and his wife was née Xu; he placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Nan 周南, courtesy name Huaxing, was registered in a military household in Jingyan County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; he was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zifu, his grandfather Yi〔a tribute student〕, his father Yong, his father’s former wife née Chen, and his mother née Li; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Bingyi, Binghe, Bingcheng, and Rang, his younger brothers Lin and Feng, and his wife née Long; he placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jian 趙鑑, courtesy name Kezheng, was registered in a military household in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junbao, his grandfather Duo, his father Fu, his mother née Li, and his stepmother née Wang; both parents were living; his elder brother was Ming and his wife née Liu; he placed nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周紀〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉善縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷理，行三，年四十，正月初二日生〕。曾祖達道，祖隲，父俊，母縻氏。永感下，兄寅、綱，娶懷氏。應天府鄉試第七十名，會試第二百三十名。

translation_en:
Zhu Yingchang, courtesy name Huiqi, was from Xiajin County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Minyi; his grandfather, Shilian, was a County Vice Magistrate; his father, Yu, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Min, and his wife was née Meng. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Jinghe, courtesy name Shiyong, was from Changsha County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, and registered in a military household of Qinzhou Guard, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Rong, his father Jun, and his mother née Cao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jingchang and Jingxin. His first wife was née Zhao, and his subsequent wife was née Zhou. He placed fifty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ji, courtesy name Tingli, was from Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty, and born on the second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Dadao, his grandfather Zhi, his father Jun, and his mother née Mi. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yin and Gang, and his wife was née Huai. He placed seventieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rong, courtesy name Dehong, was from Hezhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Yongsu, was a Medical Instructor; his grandfather was Jian, his father Li, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kuan, and his younger brothers were Ning and Zongbao. His wife was née Ma. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jin Hong, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weishen; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Xian, received the honorary title of Bureau Director; and his father, Liang, was formerly a Bureau Director in this ministry. His father's former wife, Lady Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, Lady Yuan, was granted the same title; and his stepmother was Lady Fu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huai, an Assistant Prefect, Hao, Bian, and Dan (泹) [?]; his younger brothers were Qian and Lan. He married Lady Yu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Mengying, registered in Fengdu County, Zhong Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenfu; he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wenxing; his grandfather, Hongdao, was a Daoist Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Case Reviewer; and his father, Darong, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, Lady Wu, was granted the title Lady of Service. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mengqi, a County Vice Magistrate; his younger brothers were Menglin, Qiong, Yao, and Yu. He married Lady Zhang. He placed thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Sheng, registered in Quan Subprefecture, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chengzhi; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Guan, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was An; and his father, Liang, was a County Magistrate. His mother was Lady Guo. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Bing; his younger brothers were Bian, Gao, Mian, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, and De (㝵) [?]. He married Lady Yang. He placed thirtieth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Chun, registered in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a medical household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingren; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shiheng; his grandfather, An, was a Medical Director; his father was Yun; and his mother was Lady Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gui; his younger brothers were Liu, Shi, and Shu. He married Lady Shen. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mao Ji, registered in a military household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weizhi, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was twenty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boquan, his grandfather Fuying, and his father Min, an Instructor; his father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun, Shou, and Xiu, and his wife was née Guan. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Kui, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bingwen, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingxin, his grandfather Zimao, his father Xiu, and his mother née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ming, and his wife was née Xu. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Xian, registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jishan, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was twenty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deji, his grandfather Shuyuan, and his father Shi, an Assistant Instructor in the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Lin. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Jigao, his younger brothers were Jixian and Jizhou, and his wife was née Gao. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Jian, registered in a civilian household in Linying County, Xu Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ziming, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight, born on the tenth day of the intercalary eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongneng, his grandfather Si, his father Yuan, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi and Lu, and his wife was née Gao. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

方誌〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字信之，行一，年三十六，三月初四日生〕。曾祖全翁，祖佐〔知府〕，父愚〔教諭〕，母徐氏。慈侍下，弟詒、詡、諏，娶薛氏，繼娶章氏。浙江鄉試第三十五名，會試第三百八名。
translation_en:
Peng Zan, a native of Longquan County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a military household under the Jiaozhou Battalion in Shandong. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingqi, and he ranked fourth in his family. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Defu, his grandfather Rong, his father Yuan, and his mother née Luan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ying, Li, and Jing, and his younger brother was Huan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chang, a native of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jingwen, and he ranked twentieth in his family. He was forty years old, born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Huanming, his grandfather Yunzhong, his father Suchun, and his mother née Qiu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, Wu, and Heng. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Deng. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cong, a native of Zhongbu County, Fuzhou Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dafu, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qingrong, his grandfather Zhun, his father Jing, a Chief Supervisor, and his mother née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wen, and his younger brother was Zhang. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 306th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Zhi, a native of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was registered in a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xinzhi, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-six years old, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Quanweng, his grandfather Zuo, a Prefect, his father Yu, an Instructor, and his mother née Xu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yi, Xu, and Zou. He married a woman née Xue and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Gang, registered in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Deju, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yushan, his grandfather Rangshen, his father Wenchu, and his mother Lady Chen; his father alone was still living; his younger brothers were Zai, Shan, Chong, Yuan, and Ying; he married Lady Ma and subsequently another Lady Ma; he ranked twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ji, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Jizhi, he was second in birth order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Biliang, his grandfather Yancong, his father Nan (annotation: “S磨” [思磨, an unclear title?]), his mother Lady Xie, and his stepmother Lady Yu; his father was deceased and his mother or stepmother still living; his elder brother was Ruli and his younger brothers Rugong, Rulin, Rujie, and Ruji; he married Lady Hong; he ranked twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Kun, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongyu, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Dexiang, his grandfather Wen, his father Xuan, his mother Lady Zhou, and his stepmother Lady Shen; he had surviving grandparents and parents; his younger brothers were Yan and Lun; he married Lady Zhou; he ranked one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yuqing, registered in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Congshan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gui’an, his grandfather Shangpeng, his father Dun (Assistant Instructor), and his mother Lady Li; both parents were still living; his elder brother was Lan and his younger brothers Wei and E; he married Lady Wang; he ranked twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

樊祉〔貫河南衛輝府胙城縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字介福，行三，年四十三，四月十六日生〕。曾祖通輔，祖整，父亮，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄資、興，娶段氏。河南鄉試第三十七名，會試第二百七十六名。

陳恪〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字克謹，行十三，年二十六，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖公祚，祖廷瓛〔義官〕，父斆，母吳氏。重慶下，兄愷、忱、悅、悌、性，娶朱氏。浙江鄉試第七十六名，會試第六十四名。

吳必顯〔貫直隸池州府石埭縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字德純，行一，年四十，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖妹秀，祖麟祥，父淳宗，母程氏。永感下，弟必仁、必文、必武、必達、必正，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十四名，會試第二百五名。

王資良〔貫四川成都府金堂縣，匠籍，國子生，治書經，字輔德，行三，年三十九，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖文煥，祖志道，父昇，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄資堅、資厚，娶楊氏，繼娶盧氏、趙氏。四川鄉試第二十四名，會試第二百九十三名。
translation_en:
Fan Zhi 樊祉, registered in a civilian household in Zuocheng County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jiefu, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Tongfu, his grandfather Zheng, his father Liang, and his mother née Chen; his mother alone survived, his elder brothers were Zi and Xing, and his wife was née Duan. He placed thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ke 陳恪, registered in a military household in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kejin, he ranked thirteenth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gongzuo, his grandfather Tinghuan (an honorary official), his father Xiao, and his mother née Wu; both parents and at least one grandparent were living, his elder brothers were Kai, Chen, Yue, Ti, and Xing, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Bixian 吳必顯, registered in a civilian household in Shidai County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Dechun, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Meixiu [?], his grandfather Linxiang, his father Chunzong, and his mother née Cheng; his parents and grandparents were deceased, his younger brothers were Biren, Biwen, Biwu, Bida, and Bizheng, and his wife was née Wang. He placed 134th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ziliang 王資良, registered in an artisan household in Jintang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Fude, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wenhuan, his grandfather Zhidao, his father Sheng, and his mother née Yang; his mother alone survived, his elder brothers were Zijian and Zihou, and he married a woman née Yang, followed by successive wives née Lu and née Zhao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Ziqi, registered in a salt-producing household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Mingfu, he ranked seventeenth in family order, and he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Douzhan, his grandfather Ji, his father Lu, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living. His younger brother was Ziyong. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Shao. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wei, registered in a military household in Xun County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Qingzhi, he ranked third in family order, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Shu (County Vice Magistrate), his father Chen (an honorary official), his mother née Han, and his stepmothers née Guo and née Zhang; his parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Yong (an honorary official) and Zhen (a government school student), and his younger brothers were Lan and Ji. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Cheng, registered in a military household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Xianqing, he ranked third in family order, and he was forty-three years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Danian, his grandfather Jiuling, his father Gao (Registrar of a Guard), and his mother née Li; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wan, Gao (Director of a School of Yin-yang Studies), and Ao, and his younger brothers were Xiang and Tuan. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xunbo, he ranked first in family order, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding, his grandfather Yu, his father Gu, and his mother née Zhao; both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiong, and his younger brothers were Ji (a government school student) and Yi. He married a woman née Hang. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Zi 謝諮, courtesy name Yaochen, was registered in a military household in Leiyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang; his grandfather, Bixian, was a Department Magistrate; and his father, Wenxiang, was a former Investigating Censor. His mother, née Li, was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Ne, E, Hui, Shuo, Yan, and Fang. His wife was née Cao. He placed forty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Gong 蔣恭, courtesy name Suzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Youcai; his grandfather, Fu, received the honorary title of Secretary; and his father, Yunhan, was an Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Huang, received the title of Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cong, Ming, and Cong 聰. His wife was née Hu. He placed seventieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Hou 夏鍭, courtesy name Deshu, was registered in a civilian household in Tiantai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tinggai; his grandfather, Taiyu, received the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his father, Xun, was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His mother, née Lu, received the title of Lady of Good Standing. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Qin; his younger brothers were Zi, Yue, Ting, Quan, Ling, Zan, and Gou. His wife was née Yang. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 344th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Yi 方溢, courtesy name Wenzui, was registered in a civilian household in Liucheng County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Dayong; his grandfather was Man; and his father, Sheng, was a Registrar. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hong, an Assistant Instructor; Yuan; and Qing, a sacrificial official (shengji guan) [?]. His wife was née Qin. He placed fourteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐詵〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字邦孚，行二，年四十八，十月十四日生〕。曾祖宗周，祖子珏，父性中，母朱氏。永感下，兄郁，弟譓、謐，娶吳氏，繼娶葉氏。江西鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百九十五名。
translation_en:
Hao Ben, registered in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Lifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather’s name is recorded as 𨱆 [?]; his father was Ji, a Ceremonial Escort; and his mother was the Lady of Wutai Commandery. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Lun, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Kai. He married Lady Jiang. He placed forty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Liangxuan, registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Fuhua; he ranked twenty-third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shiyong, his grandfather Xianmo, his father Yucheng, and his mother Lady Wen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Liang’an. He married Lady He. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qi, registered in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingzhao; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather was Qin, an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang; his father was Ben; his legal mother was Lady Zheng; and his birth mother was Lady Huang. Parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jiao and Huan, and his younger brother was Gen. He was betrothed to Lady Yang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shen, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zongzhou, his grandfather Zijue, his father Xingzhong, and his mother Lady Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yu, and his younger brothers were Hui and Mi. He married Lady Wu and subsequently Lady Ye. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Bing, courtesy name Wenhuan, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, his birth order, age, and birth month are garbled in the transcription [?]; he was born on the twenty-fifth day. His great-grandfather was Bowu, posthumously appointed Secretary; his grandfather was Shi, a Prefect; his father was Xiao, Office Manager in the Nanjing Hanlin Academy; and his mother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ren and Xiang, and he married Lady Hu. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Tingbin, courtesy name Shangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was seventh in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Caizhi; his grandfather, Hangao; his father, Xuqin; and his mother, Lady He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qi, an Assistant Instructor, and Zhou. He married Lady Zeng and subsequently Lady Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wei, courtesy name Jiayu, was registered in an official household of Suzhou Guard in the directly administered region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shengyuan; his grandfather was Gang, an Instructor; his father was Yuan; and his mother was Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Can, and he married Lady Wang. He placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yin, courtesy name Tingzhang, was registered in a military household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Rixin; his grandfather, Shenghu; his father, Kui; and his mother, Lady Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jia, and his younger brothers were Fu and Gun. He married Lady Yi. He placed thirty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wei Hou, registered in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanzai; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Honghai, his grandfather Kegong, and his father Ling; his mother and stepmother were both née Qian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jian, Sheng, Xi, Fu, Fu, Gen, Meng, Kun, Ji, Kan, and Yu [the division of the unpunctuated names is uncertain]. His wife was née Wu. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan, registered in Haifeng County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingyong; he ranked tenth in his family and was twenty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Pu was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Virtue, Senior Minister of Correct Governance, and Minister of Revenue. His grandfather Zuo held those same titles and was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Junior Guardian, with the posthumous name Zhongjian. His father Yu was an Honorary Official, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu (authorized to wear official cap and girdle), Xuan (an Honorary Official), Xi, Mao, Yan, Qi, Kun, Rui, Yu, and Yang; his younger brothers were Zhen, Xiu, and Gong. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kan, registered in Leping County, Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongyue; he ranked first in his family and was forty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De, his grandfather Jizhong (authorized under applicable regulations to wear official cap and girdle), and his father Ning; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Heng, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Yong, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry. His courtesy name was Sicheng; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-nine, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongcai, his grandfather Minxu, and his father Xuan, an Instructor; his mother was née Peng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhuan, Shun, and Po, and his wife was née Bao. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zeng Yi, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shichao; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Se’an, his grandfather Wanzhen, his father Boding, and his mother Lady Wang; both parents were living. His younger brother was Rong, and he married Lady Huang. He placed eighty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yingqi, registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Wenrui; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongwen, his grandfather Zhou, an Assistant Prefect, and his father Sheng, a County Magistrate; his mother was Lady Wu and his stepmother Lady Lei. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married Lady Yang and subsequently Lady Xing. He placed thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Jue, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingyong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged fifty, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongjie, his grandfather Shilian, his father Jingyong, and his mother Lady Qian; both parents were deceased. He married Lady Xu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Zhong, registered in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanxiao; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziying, his grandfather Andao, and his father Gao; his mother was Lady Yin and his stepmother Lady Yao. His mother was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving father. His younger brother was Shu, and he married Lady Zhao. He placed one hundred twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
華璉〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字商器，行一，年二十三，六月二十九日生〕。曾祖孟學〔國子監學正〕，祖冕〔訓導〕，父麟，母孫氏。重慶下，弟玨、璪、璀，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第六十二名，會試第二百六十二名。

蔣浤〔貫應天府上元縣官籍，直隸長洲縣人，國子生，治書經，字維深，行一，年四十三，五月十九日生〕。曾祖文德，祖善〔通判〕，父瓛，母王氏。嚴侍下，弟淮、澗，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第十九名，會試第二名。

徐璘〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣人，山東登州衛軍籍，國子生，治書經，字文璧，行五，年三十七，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖福肆，祖添福，父能，前母吳氏、吳氏，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄琮、璟、瑛、珍，弟瑾、璋、瓚，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第二百二十九名。
translation_en:
Hua Lian, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shangqi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengxue, Instructor at the National University; his grandfather was Mian, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Lin, and his mother was née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Jue, Zao, and Cui, and he married a woman née Shen. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Hong, registered in an official household in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and originally from Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weishen; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-three, and was born on the nineteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wende; his grandfather was Shan, an Assistant Prefect; his father was Huan, and his mother was née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Huai and Jian, and he married a woman née Yang. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhi Kui, registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kejing; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keli; his grandfather was Qi; his father was Yan, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lan and his younger brother was Fan, and he married a woman née Zhao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Lin, originally from Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a military household of the Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenbi; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fusi; his grandfather was Tianfu; and his father was Neng. His father's former wife is listed as née Wu, followed by another 'née Wu' [?]; his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Cong, Jing, Ying, and Zhen; his younger brothers were Jin, Zhang, and Zan; and he married a woman née Liu. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Guan 王貫 was a native of Rongchang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, registered as a guardsman in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Yizhi and ranked second among his brothers; he was thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Hanqing, his grandfather Yong, his father Qi, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chong, and his younger brothers were Kuang and Chun. He married a woman née Xu. He placed twenty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Zuo 袁佐 was registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Anlu Subprefecture, Huguang. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Guozuo and ranked first among his brothers; he was thirty-four, born on the second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Min, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; his grandfather was Shixian, his father Mian, and his mother née Wen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was You. He married a woman née Xie. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Ai 沈昹 was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he had the courtesy name Yuanzhong and ranked fifth among his brothers; he was thirty-five, born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather Ming had been granted the honorary title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; and his father Xiang was an Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father's former wife, née Qu, had been posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother was née Wang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhong, Hou, Jian, who held an honorary official title for charitable service, and Mo. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed thirty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Che Fen 車份 was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Wenyi and ranked third among his brothers; he was forty-two, born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Boda, his grandfather Chun, his father Yue, and his mother née Ma. His mother alone was living. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.
